Performance monitors complement flow monitors in CloudWatch Network Monitoring. When a checkout application slows down, a performance monitor shows whether the path from the web tier in one Availability Zone to the database in another is degraded. A high network impact score points to the AWS network
title: Amazon CloudWatch simplifies network performance monitoring for your Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)

summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports database-internal audit logging, a fully managed capability that captures SQL statements executed on your cluster. Previously, AWS CloudTrail recorded who connected to a DSQL cluster, but not what they did once inside it. Now, financial institutions and regulated enterprises can meet production compliance requirements by capturing DDL, DML, DCL, and SELECT statements with full statement text, bind parameters, acting principal (both PostgreSQL role and AWS IAM identity), timestamp, table name, and transaction identifier. With audit logging, you can feed SIEM systems directly from Amazon S3, satisfy auditor requirements for change accountability, and reconstruct events after security incidents. Logs are delivered as structured JSON to your S3 bucket via CloudWatch Vended Logs. Configuration requires a single SQL setting—no extension to load and no log-shipping pipeline to build. Audit logging is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available. Audit logging will incur Aurora DSQL DPU charges, charges for log delivery through CloudWatch Logs, and charges for storing audit records in Amazon S3. For pricing information, see Aurora DSQL pricing . To learn more, see audit logging in the Aurora DSQL User Guide.
title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports audit logging

summary: AWS Clean Rooms now supports intermediate tables for PySpark jobs , offering increased flexibility for organizations running complex, multi-step analytical workflows with their partners. With this launch, customers can write the results of a PySpark job to an intermediate table for reuse in subsequent analyses. For example, a measurement vendor can perform feature engineering with PySpark, then use those results as input into an ML model training job to identify new high-value customers to inform audience targeting and bid optimization for their campaigns. AWS Clean Rooms helps companies and their partners easily analyze and collaborate on their collective datasets without revealing or copying one another’s underlying data. For more information about the AWS Regions where AWS Clean Rooms is available, see the AWS Regions table. To learn more about collaborating with AWS Clean Rooms, visit AWS Clean Rooms .
title: AWS Clean Rooms supports writing PySpark job results to intermediate tables

summary: Amazon CloudFront Functions can now make network calls and act on the response during a request. CloudFront Functions runs lightweight JavaScript at CloudFront edge locations to customize requests and responses. Previously, if your logic depended on data from another service, you had to use Lambda@Edge or move that logic to your origin. Now your functions can use real-time data to personalize, authenticate, or route requests at the edge, close to your viewers. With the new cf.fetch() method, your functions can call your API endpoints and use the response to decide how to handle each request. For example, you can check an AI agent's permissions and usage budget so that only authorized requests reach your API or MCP server, or send request signals to a security or fraud detection service to block or challenge bad traffic. With cf.beacon() , you can send analytics events in the background without slowing down viewers, even for content served from cache. Both methods take advantage of the origin settings already on your distribution, including origin access control (OAC), VPC origins, and connection reuse. Network calls are available at all CloudFront edge locations. They cost $0.10 per million calls, on top of CloudFront Functions invocation charges, and are included at no additional cost in the Pro plan and above in CloudFront flat-rate plans. To learn more, see Helper methods for network calls in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide and Amazon CloudFront pricing .
title: Amazon CloudFront Functions now supports network calls

summary: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Hybrid Nodes now has lower pricing for large nodes, capping the billed vCPU per node at 32 vCPU, so you are no longer charged for vCPUs above that per node threshold. Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes lets you use your existing on-premises and edge infrastructure as nodes in Amazon EKS clusters. You can now use your largest servers, including those with GPUs, with Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes at lower cost. With this change, the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes cost of a large server no longer grows with its vCPU count. At the first pricing tier, a 64 vCPU node now costs 50% less than before, and a 256 vCPU node costs 88% less, as both are now billed only for 32 vCPUs. This makes Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes more cost-effective for large bare-metal and GPU servers running compute-intensive workloads, such as AI/ML training and inference, that must stay on-premises for data residency, latency, or regulatory reasons. The pricing change applies automatically to all new hybrid nodes. For the new pricing to take effect for existing hybrid nodes attached to clusters, delete and reattach them. Nodes with 32 vCPUs or fewer are still billed for their actual vCPUs, and existing tiered pricing still applies, so your effective rate falls as monthly usage grows. The new pricing is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes is available. To learn more about getting started and updated pricing details, visit the Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes documentation and Ama
title: Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes reduces price for large hosts

summary: Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL major version 9.7, the latest Long-Term Support release from MySQL community. Amazon RDS for MySQL 9.7 launches with community MySQL 9.7.4. This launch introduces support for the Replication Applier Metrics component, JSON Duality Views, and Hypergraph Optimizer. The Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction. JSON Duality Views let applications read and write the same relational tables as JSON documents. The Hypergraph Optimizer is an opt-in query optimizer that can improve execution plans for complex, multi-join queries. For more details, refer to the MySQL 9.7.4 release notes and the Amazon RDS for MySQL release notes . You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments , in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon RDS User Guide . This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for MySQL is available. Learn more about pricing details at Amazon RDS for MySQL pricing . Amazon RDS for MySQL makes it simple to set up, operate, and scale MySQL deployments in the cloud. Create or update a fully managed Amazon RDS database in the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).
title: Amazon RDS for MySQL now supports MySQL major version 9.7

summary: Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports additional access log fields that were previously available only in CloudFront real-time logs. You can now include these fields in your standard logs and deliver them to Amazon S3, Amazon CloudWatch Logs, or Amazon Data Firehose, without setting up an additional data stream for real-time logs. The new fields include the IP address of the CloudFront server that handled the request, identifiers that separate traffic on a primary distribution from traffic on a staging distribution, and a media quality confidence score. They also include Common Media Client Data (CMCD) fields, which video players send with each request to report details like bitrate, buffer length, and playback session ID. Streaming teams can use these fields to match playback problems that viewers see with CloudFront delivery data, which makes troubleshooting faster. These fields are available in all CloudFront edge locations, and standard logging pricing applies. To learn more, see Standard logging page in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide .
title: Amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports CMCD and additional log fields

summary: AWS Transform custom now enables you to share transformation definitions (TDs) and their associated lessons across AWS accounts, organizational units (OUs), or your entire organization in AWS Organizations through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). AWS Transform custom is a capability of AWS Transform that performs transformations across your technology stack, including API and framework upgrades, migrations, and language translations. With this launch, you can share TDs as live resources rather than static copies, so consumers run the owner's latest published version by default while the owner maintains full control. As the TD owner, you select from four managed permissions ranging from execute-only (the default) to permissions that allow consumers to use your lessons, contribute lessons back to you, or download the TD. Lessons flow back to the owner only when the permission allows it and the consumer opts in. This capability is particularly valuable for platform engineering teams and AWS Partners who need to deploy standardized transformations across multiple accounts. A central team can create a TD once and share it organization-wide. This feature is available via the AWS Transform CLI and AWS RAM in US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Canada (Central) Regions. To learn more, visit the AWS Transform User Guide .
title: AWS Transform custom now supports cross-account sharing of transformation definitions

summary: Today, Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced version 1.0 of ExtendDB, the first release of the open source Amazon DynamoDB-compatible adapter for production use. ExtendDB is fully compatible with the DynamoDB API and runs on a database backend that you choose, so developers and infrastructure teams can run DynamoDB workloads in on-premises data centers, in private or public clouds, and at the edge without rewriting application code. ExtendDB 1.0 supports four storage backends, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra, and MongoDB. For local development and continuous integration (CI), the extenddb-dev container image and the @extenddb/dev npm package run a DynamoDB-compatible endpoint over SQLite, so you don’t have to set up an external database. ExtendDB is maintained by AWS, released under the Apache 2.0 license, and developed in the open on GitHub. To learn more, see the ExtendDB project page . To get started or contribute, visit the GitHub repository .
title: AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0

summary: Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces cross-Region inference routing, which helps keep inference applications available when a region runs short of capacity by sending requests to endpoints deployed in other AWS Regions and AWS accounts. Models served on accelerated instances can reach capacity limits in a single Region, and an unhealthy endpoint can lead to throttling and errors for end users. Previously, teams had to build and maintain their own routing, health checks, and retry logic across Regions. With cross-Region inference routing in SageMaker AI, developers create an inference router, register the real-time endpoints, asynchronous endpoints, and inference components they already run, and point their applications at the router. The router prefers endpoints in its own Region, shifts new requests to healthy destinations in other Regions as errors rise, and returns traffic gradually after the local endpoint recovers. Existing endpoints, models, and containers do not change. Endpoint owners stay in control: an endpoint policy determines which routers in other accounts can use an endpoint, and an optional cross-Region traffic cap reserves capacity for the endpoint’s local callers. Each real-time response identifies the endpoint that served the request and the reason, and router metrics in Amazon CloudWatch show where traffic went. Cross-Region inference routing is available for real-time inference in 32 commercial AWS Regions, and for asynchronous inference in 25 Regions. Th
title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports cross-Region inference routing

summary: AWS Glue ETL now offers the Apache Spark Optimization Agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and delivers cost and performance optimization recommendations within minutes. You can select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns specific configuration changes with the telemetry evidence and reasoning behind each suggestion. You can use the agent on any completed job run from the AWS Glue console, or from your own tools through the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio MCP Server. The agent takes the job's configuration, logs, and Spark telemetry together with your chosen goal and returns recommendations computed by a deterministic recommendation engine. The engine reads all job artifacts together to identify what is driving runtime and cost: too little parallelism, a skewed join key, memory pressure forcing spill, idle executors, or capacity provisioned beyond what the job uses. When cost and performance trade off, the agent improves the metric you chose while keeping any regression of the other within defined limits. The engine also checks best practices such as platform-level improvements like upgrading to a newer AWS Glue version or using AWS Graviton processors. Each recommendation is labeled by the area it modifies: infrastructure, Spark configuration, code, or data layout. All access is authenticated with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and logged in AWS CloudTrail. The Apache Spark Optimization Agent is available at no additional charge for AWS Glue
title: Introducing the Apache Spark Optimization Agent for AWS Glue ETL

summary: Today, AWS announced the general availability of Amazon OpenSearch Memory, a new serverless capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service for adding persistent memory to AI agents. OpenSearch Memory stores agent interactions as searchable events, derives useful memories, and retrieves relevant context across sessions, so agents can recall prior decisions, earlier interactions, and user preferences without replaying the full conversation history to the model. Customers can give agents long-term memory without provisioning infrastructure or building separate extraction, indexing, consolidation, and retrieval systems. OpenSearch Memory stores the original events verbatim, makes them searchable within seconds, and asynchronously derives structured memories. It manages the full memory lifecycle, including extraction, embedding, indexing, consolidation (adding, updating, or skipping memories as new information arrives), and retrieval using keyword, semantic, and hybrid search. Customers control access with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) for each memory store, with actor and session scoping, and can set expiration periods for events and memories. Because it is serverless, there are no clusters to provision, instance types to choose, or indexes to create, and capacity for extraction and search scales automatically. Amazon OpenSearch Memory is available today in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Regions. For pricing details
title: Amazon OpenSearch Memory is now generally available

summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support privileged mode, which lets your agents install system-level software and run nested containers. Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. You turn on privileged mode when you create or update an agent runtime that runs on runtime instances. For example, a coding agent can start its service dependencies, such as Postgres and Redis, as containers and run its integration tests against them. A code-modernization agent can install the compilers and libraries that a migration needs. A session that runs a privileged agent runs only that agent, so elevated privileges stay with one agent on its instance. Agents that don't use privileged mode keep the default standard mode, so existing agents don't change. Standard mode suits most agents. Use privileged mode only if your agent needs to install system-level software or run containers. Privileged mode is available in all AWS Regions where AgentCore runtime instances are available. To get started, see the following resources: Configure the privilege mode for runtime instances in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide AgentCore pricing
title: AgentCore runtime instances now support privileged mode

summary: AWS Deadline Cloud now supports Amazon EC2 G7 instances in service-managed fleets. Deadline Cloud is a fully managed service that helps teams run compute-intensive workloads for visual effects, animation, product design, simulation, and gaming. G7 instances give customers more options to scale GPU capacity quickly. You can add G7 instances to your service-managed fleets in sizes from g7.2xlarge to g7.48xlarge, with On-Demand or Spot pricing on Linux or Windows workers. This lets you scale GPU rendering capacity to match your production schedule without managing your own render farm infrastructure. To get started, create or update a service-managed fleet in the Deadline Cloud console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs, and select the RTX PRO 4500 GPU accelerator. G7 instances are available in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), and Asia Pacific (Sydney) Regions. To learn more, see Use a GPU accelerator in the AWS Deadline Cloud User Guide .
title: AWS Deadline Cloud now supports Amazon EC2 G7 instances in service-managed fleets

summary: AWS HealthOmics now supports Nextflow version 26.10, which adds enhancements such as static typing, pipeline composition, and configurable report directories. AWS HealthOmics is a HIPAA-eligible service that helps healthcare and life sciences customers accelerate scientific breakthroughs at scale with fully managed bioinformatics workflows. In Nextflow 26.10, static typing lets workflow developers declare types for parameters, inputs, and outputs, and the nextflow lint command reports type errors before any task is submitted. Pipeline composition lets developers include a statically typed pipeline from their workflow package and call it like a sub-workflow, so validated pipelines can be reused as building blocks. For example, you can include an alignment pipeline and a variant-calling pipeline in one workflow, and each sample moves to variant calling as soon as alignment finishes. Collection parameters can now be loaded directly from CSV, JSON, or YAML sample sheets into record types. Execution reports, timelines, and traces can be written to a directory inside the workflow output, and HealthOmics exports them with the run outputs. You can use Nextflow 26.10 in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London), Israel (Tel Aviv), and Asia Pacific (Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo). To learn more, visit the Nextflow version release notes documentation.
title: AWS HealthOmics now supports Nextflow version 26.10

summary: AWS DevOps Agent now supports dedicated Slack code channels and two-way conversations in Microsoft Teams, so on-call engineers and DevOps teams can investigate and resolve incidents where they already work together. AWS DevOps Agent investigates incidents across AWS, multicloud, and on-premises environments. Slack code channels give each investigation its own channel. Choose Open in code channel on an investigation card, and your team and the agent work on the investigation together in that channel. You can ask follow-up questions without @mentioning the agent. If you registered your Slack workspace before this launch, update your Slack permissions to use code channels. For Microsoft Teams, before this launch, users received only one-way notifications from AWS DevOps Agent. Now you can mention AWS DevOps Agent in a connected private or shared channel to ask questions, explore your AWS resources, and steer investigations. The agent replies in a thread under your message. To get started, turn on Bidirectional mode when you associate the channel with your Agent Space. A channel member then authorizes the association before the agent posts. These capabilities are available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS DevOps Agent is currently supported. To get started, see the following resources: Using Slack code channels Connecting Microsoft Teams AWS DevOps Agent product page
title: AWS DevOps Agent now supports Slack code channels and Microsoft Teams two-way conversations

summary: Amazon Braket now offers a new device status, PAUSED, to give customers clear and actionable information on when they can submit quantum tasks and hybrid jobs and when those tasks and jobs will run. Device status now tells you: ONLINE: The device is accepting quantum tasks and hybrid jobs and is actively processing them during its availability window. (New) PAUSED: The device is accepting quantum tasks and hybrid jobs but isn't processing them right now, because it is outside its availability window, in short-term maintenance, or in a reservation. Tasks and jobs you submit stay QUEUED and run once the device is ONLINE. OFFLINE: The device is unavailable and isn't accepting new quantum tasks or hybrid jobs, for example due to scheduled maintenance, upgrades, or operational issues. RETIRED: The device has been permanently decommissioned and is no longer available on Amazon Braket. When a device is PAUSED, a Status Reason is provided with additional information on why it's paused, when the status began, and an estimated end time if one is available. You can view device status on the Devices page in the Amazon Braket console, or programmatically with the GetDevice and SearchDevices APIs or the Amazon Braket SDK. For example, the GetDevice API will return one of the following status reasons for PAUSED state: OUTSIDE_AVAILABILITY_WINDOW, MAINTENANCE, or RESERVATION. Amazon Braket is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Europe (London),
title: Amazon Braket adds PAUSED device status

summary: Today, AWS AppConfig introduces two new configuration profile types to help you manage the settings for your generative AI applications: AI model invocation configurations, and AI prompt configurations. You can now change model settings and prompts while your application is running, without redeploying code. These updates use AWS AppConfig's safe deployment practices, including gradual rollouts and automatic rollback. This can allow you to move faster and safer, and avoid unexpected behaviors and tokenomics results with rapidly evolving AI solutions. AI model invocation configurations store the settings your application uses to call an AI model. These include the model identifier, inference parameters such as temperature and maximum tokens, and messages such as system prompts and example conversation turns. Provider-specific options are managed in custom parameters, so the same schema works across AI providers. Similarly, AI prompt configurations store prompts as separately versioned artifacts. You can update and optimize a prompt on its own,without changing the model configuration, and reuse it across multiple applications. This allows for powerful prompt engineering. You can roll out a change to these gradually, for example to 10%, then 20%, then 30% of your traffic. Along the way, you can measure the change's effect on operational metrics, customer experience, and token usage. If an alarm in Amazon CloudWatch, Datadog, New Relic, or another observability solution goes off
title: AWS AppConfig launches support for managing native AI model and AI prompt configuration

summary: AWS Transform now automates the tasks that prepare and validate your servers during a migration, before they move and after they launch on AWS. AWS Transform is the agentic AI service that speeds up cloud migration, application modernization, and continuous tech debt reduction. With the new source actions capability, you can create actions and run them securely on your source servers at the right point in the migration, from the early stages through cutover. Post-launch actions complement this by automatically configuring and validating each workload as soon as it launches on AWS. Cutover preparation and validation are often manual, time-consuming tasks in large-scale migrations. Traditionally, migration teams log in to each source server to stop services and freeze database writes before shutdown, and then check connectivity, application health, and monitoring on each server after it launches. With source actions in AWS Transform, you define each action once, run it in bulk on the servers and waves you choose, and reuse it across accounts and migrations. AWS Transform manages these actions centrally, so you can reuse them across accounts and migrations instead of rebuilding them each time. You can monitor the status of each action and confirm your go/no-go decision before moving to the next step. Source preparation and post-launch actions are now part of the migration plan itself, so you no longer have to coordinate and run these activities by hand. This capability is availa
title: AWS Transform automates source and migration target actions to accelerate cutover

summary: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances, so operations teams can start tracking and resolving customer issues on day one without any setup work. New instances come with Cases connected to rules for setting SLAs, Customer Profiles for personalizing customer experiences, and Amazon EventBridge for triggering actions in other business applications when a case is updated. Administrators of existing instances can enable these integrations with one click in the AWS Management Console. Newly added case fields sync automatically, so admins don't have to update integrations each time they create fields. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .
title: Amazon Connect Customer enables Cases by default for new instances

summary: AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS announces Account Tagging for SaaS Products for AWS Revenue Measurement. Partners can now measure the AWS revenue impact of their SaaS solutions by tagging the AWS accounts that host them, instead of tagging individual resources. Until now, Partners with SaaS listings measured that impact through Resource Tagging, User Agent strings, or AWS Marketplace Metering. With Account Tagging for SaaS products, a Partner uses AWS Organizations to tag partner-owned member accounts dedicated to a single SaaS product. The tag key is aws-apn-id-<partner-central-aws-account-id> and the tag value is pc:<AWS Marketplace product-code>. AWS Revenue Measurement then attributes all eligible AWS consumption in each tagged account to that product. Account Tagging for SaaS Products is available for products with a SaaS listing on AWS Marketplace. Each tagged account must be dedicated to one product. Partners whose products share an account can continue to use Resource Tagging, User Agent string, or Identity Tagging. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more about implementing AWS Revenue Measurement, review the onboarding guide for more information.
title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports Account Tagging for SaaS Products

summary: Developers on Amazon WorkSpaces Personal can now turn on Nested Virtualization for their own WorkSpaces from the Windows WorkSpaces client, without asking an administrator to make each change. Once an administrator grants self-service permission for the directory, developers can run Docker Desktop, Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2), and Android emulators directly on their WorkSpaces. Administrators can now grant a directory-level self-service permission for Nested Virtualization. Once granted, end users can turn the setting on or off for their own Windows WorkSpace from the WorkSpaces client. Administrators keep control because the permission is set per directory. Self-service is supported on WorkSpaces Personal, using the Desktop Cloud Visualization (DCV) protocol, on Standard bundles and higher. Power (4 vCPU) or higher is recommended. Value and Graphics bundles are not supported. Nested virtualization is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon WorkSpaces is available, excluding the China (Ningxia) Region. There is no additional charge for supported bundles. For more information, visit the Amazon WorkSpaces documentation on Nested Virtualization . For pricing, visit the Amazon WorkSpaces pricing page .
title: Amazon WorkSpaces now lets developers enable Nested Virtualization

summary: Customers can now use Amazon EC2 performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring to observe and act on the performance of their EC2 workloads without setup within the instance, complementing their in-guest tooling. Customers running performance-sensitive EC2 workloads can use these signals to monitor their CPU and GPU resources, tune capacity needs, and troubleshoot application issues. EC2 performance status checks identify nonterminal hardware conditions that impact performance on accelerated computing instances. These checks also recommend an action, such as rebooting to complete GPU memory row remapping without replacing the instance. The additions to Detailed Monitoring include support for OpenTelemetry metrics, one-minute GPU metrics that help teams tune accelerated workloads, and a new, higher resolution 10-second CPU utilization metric that helps customers size and scale compute capacity using EC2 Application Auto Scaling. Customers can selectively opt into these new metrics using categories that they can easily apply to their instances across their fleet. Together, these new capabilities make it easier for customers to manage their compute resources. EC2 performance status checks are available at no additional charge. EC2 Detailed Monitoring metrics are opt-in and incur standard CloudWatch charges for EC2 Detailed Monitoring. These capabilities are available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn mor
title: Amazon EC2 launches performance status checks and new utilization metrics for EC2 Detailed Monitoring

summary: AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS announces Identity Tagging in AWS Revenue Measurement, a new way for Partners to get attributed revenue visibility for the AWS usage their solutions drive. Partners can now tag the IAM user or role their solution uses instead of tagging individual resources or decorating individual SDK/API calls. This makes attribution simpler and needs no code changes. Until now, Partners using Resource Tagging had to apply tags to each resource their solution created or managed. That could be hard to keep consistent across customer environments. With Identity Tagging, Partners apply a tag to the IAM role or user their solution uses in the AWS account. AWS Revenue Measurement then attributes usage from resources created by that identity to the Partner's product. Identity Tagging works alongside existing methods such as Resource Tagging, User Agent string, and SaaS Account Tagging, so Partners can pick the method that best fits their architecture. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more, review the AWS Revenue Measurement onboarding guide .
title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports Identity Tagging

summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of the open source AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust. Rust developers can use the SDK to build resilient, long-running workflows using Lambda durable functions, to create multi-step applications like infrastructure automation, deployment rollouts with approval gates, and pipelines that call AI models and pause for human review directly in their Rust code without implementing custom progress tracking. Lambda durable functions extend Lambda's event-driven programming model with operations that checkpoint progress automatically and pause execution for up to one year when waiting on external events. With the SDK, developers write a durable function as an ordinary async Rust function that awaits each durable operation like any other future and can run independent operations concurrently. The SDK includes steps that save their results, callbacks for human-in-the-loop and agent-in-the-loop workflows, invocations of other durable functions, and timed waits. The SDK works with the Rust tools developers already use. Developers add the aws-durable-execution-sdk crate with cargo add, build with Cargo Lambda, and deploy a single binary on the provided.al2023 runtime. Before deploying, they can test complete workflows with cargo test and the SDK's LocalRunner without requiring network access or AWS credentials. To get started, see the Lambda durable functions developer guide , the Rust SDK guide , and the AWS Lambda Durable Execution SD
title: AWS Lambda Durable Execution SDK for Rust is now generally available

summary: AWS Health now supports resource and account tags in Health events. This new capability enables you to enrich Health events with resource tags and account tags, providing additional context to help you manage and respond to events more effectively. With this feature, you can now view resource tags directly within Health events for supported AWS services. This allows you to quickly identify which resources are affected and understand their business context without needing to navigate to individual service consoles. Additionally, account-level tags help you categorize and filter events across your organization, making it easier to route notifications and automate responses based on your organizational structure. This enhancement is particularly valuable for organizations managing large-scale AWS deployments. By leveraging tags in Health events, you can streamline incident response workflows, improve cost allocation tracking for health-related events, and enable more granular event filtering in AWS Health Dashboard and AWS Health API responses. The feature integrates seamlessly with Amazon EventBridge, allowing you to create event-driven automation that responds to tagged resources and accounts. This enables sophisticated routing and handling of Health events based on tag values, supporting use cases such as automatically creating tickets in your IT service management system or sending targeted notifications to specific teams. To enable tag enrichment, visit the AWS Health Dashb
title: AWS Health now supports resource and account tags

summary: Today, AWS Marketplace announces the general availability of buyer approvals. This lets you decide which AWS Marketplace purchases need sign-off, who approves them, and where approval happens. You can define buying policies for the conditions that matter to you, such as purchase amount, product type, pricing, and whether an offer is public or private. Additionally, you can choose to route each purchase request to the right place: the AWS Marketplace console, a chain of approvers by email, or your procurement system in Coupa or SAP Ariba. When you route approvals by email, procurement, finance, legal, and cloud governance teams can approve requests without needing to sign into the AWS console. They see the product, price, terms, and can approve right from their email. For example, you can route large software commitments to Coupa or SAP Ariba for review, send mid-size purchases to multiple approvers by email, and let low-cost or pay-as-you-go purchases go through without approval. When a purchase is routed to your procurement system, it follows your existing approval flows and gets a dedicated purchase order for cleaner spend tracking and reconciliation. With AWS Marketplace, customers can already choose which subset of available products their teams can buy, track each purchase with purchase orders, and require their employees to enter a purchase order when buying. Now, with buyer approvals, you can also control how each purchase is approved before making a financial commitme
title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer approval workflows

summary: AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) provides measurement of AWS consumption driven by Partner solutions. Today, AWS announces expanded Amazon Bedrock support in AWS Revenue Measurement. Partners can now gain attributed revenue visibility for their solutions' use of closed-source models in Amazon Bedrock, giving them a more complete view of the revenue their solutions drive. Until now, only Amazon models (such as Amazon Nova) and open-weight models in Amazon Bedrock were included in AWS Revenue Measurement. With this update, attributed revenue for Amazon Bedrock reflects the total Bedrock charges, including closed-source model usage. Partners who already use Resource Tagging, User Agent string, Identity Tagging, or SaaS Account Tagging for Amazon Bedrock automatically benefit from the expanded coverage, with no additional implementation needed. AWS Revenue Measurement is generally available in all commercial regions. To learn more, review the Amazon Bedrock best practices in the AWS Revenue Measurement onboarding guide.
title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports closed-source models in Amazon Bedrock

summary: AWS Transform for migrations now recommends the optimized storage type and configuration for every server you migrate, so you no longer do it server by server. Building on recent storage assessment capabilities , AWS Transform's recommendations use each server's observed performance and capacity data to reduce overprovisioning costs and avoid performance issues after cutover. You see the expected cost before you migrate, and AWS Transform applies the approved settings automatically at launch. Recommendations cover Amazon EBS and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. For FSx for NetApp ONTAP, they include the file system layout and sizing. You choose whether to optimize for cost or for performance, and recommendations stay consistent from assessment through launch. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform for migrations is available . To learn more, see the AWS Transform user guide .
title: AWS Transform supports optimized storage for server migration

summary: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store has increased the default throughput limits for five API operations. For accounts that have turned on the higher throughput setting, the quotas have changed as follows, in transactions per second (TPS): GetParametersByPath (from 100 to 500 TPS) PutParameter (10 to 50) DeleteParameter (5 to 50) DescribeParameters (10 to 100) GetParameterHistory (10 to 100) Parameter Store provides powerful, hierarchical storage for configuration data. The higher quotas give more headroom to workloads that call these operations in bursts. Examples include applications that load configuration by path when many AWS Lambda functions start at once, infrastructure as code deployments that create or update many parameters, and cleanup jobs that bulk-delete stale parameters.
title: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store raises API throughput limits

summary: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing. When customers subscribe to a third-party product, they can share their contact information with the seller. This helps sellers onboard new customers, send deployment guides and setup instructions, provide technical support, and share product updates from the start of the subscription. Customers share their first name, last name, email address, company name, and country or region in the deployment contact information section of the AWS Marketplace procurement page. AWS Marketplace pre-fills this section from the customer's previous purchases, AWS Profile , or AWS account details where available, so customers don't need to enter it again for each subscription. Customers can complete or edit any field before they subscribe, and view what they shared on the agreement details page in the AWS Marketplace console. Sellers can view the customer's contact information on the agreement details page in AWS Partner Central, or retrieve it with the new GetAgreementContacts API to bring it into their onboarding and support workflows. Sellers of software as a service (SaaS) products can call the API to pre-fill their registration page, so customers confirm their details instead of entering them again. This capability is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To learn more, see Sharing your contact information at subscription in the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide and Receiving buyer contact information in t
title: AWS Marketplace now supports buyer contact sharing at subscription

summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL now lets you create multi-Region clusters whose Regions are on different continents, such as US East (N. Virginia) and Europe (Ireland). Until now, the Regions in a multi-Region cluster had to be in the same geographic Region set. With intercontinental multi-Region clusters, applications on two continents read and write to one strongly consistent database. If a Region becomes unavailable, committed writes are preserved and applications keep reading and writing in the other Region. You choose the two peer Regions and the witness Region. Place your database close to users on each continent, or separate failure domains as widely as your resilience needs require. Intercontinental multi-Region clusters are available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL supports multi-Region clusters. To learn more, see Multi-Region cluster availability in the Aurora DSQL User Guide.
title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports multi-Region peering across continents

summary: Amazon MSK Connect (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect) now supports restarting both existing and newly created connectors and their tasks in place, enabling fast recovery for streaming data pipelines. Amazon MSK Connect is a fully managed service that allows you to deploy, monitor, and scale Apache Kafka Connect connectors with Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). Previously, recovering from failures required deleting and recreating the connector, resulting in downtime and operational overhead. With this feature, you can restart your connector and all its tasks in place, or selectively restart only the failed tasks, making recovery seamless. You can also restart connectors that have no failed tasks to recover from transient issues or to pick up changes in external systems or dependencies. This restart capability is available at no additional cost through the Amazon MSK Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDK, and AWS CDK in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Connect is available. To learn more, visit the Amazon MSK Connect documentation . To get started, visit the Amazon MSK Console .
title: Amazon MSK Connect now supports restarting existing connectors

summary: AWS Marketplace search, Agent Mode, and AWS sales teams use listings to recommend partner offerings to AWS customers. Partners who sell software and services can now create and improve their listings in AWS Partner Central with the new AI-assisted listing experience. It drafts content from a partner's website and other materials, then shows which sections need clearer details, use cases, or evidence of customer outcomes. For single-AMI products, it also drafts the usage instructions buyers see after subscribing. Partners see, for each section, whether it meets what buyers look for, and choose which suggestions to use and review all content before publishing. Partners can position products and professional services as distinct solutions for different industries, use cases, or outcomes. Each solution gets its own AWS Marketplace page, bringing its case studies and AWS Specializations together with the listing's pricing, reviews, and trust information, so buyers can evaluate and buy from the same page. Buyers can filter search results by Specialization. Partners not ready to share public pricing can publish without it using leads-only listings, through which interested customers request a private offer that reaches the partner as a lead in AWS Partner Central. Partners can test metering and billing setup before publishing, and ask the assistant metering questions while integrating. These capabilities are available now to AWS Marketplace partners in all AWS Regions, except the AW
title: AWS Partner Central now supports AI-assisted listing experience for product, services, and solutions

summary: AWS Elemental MediaTailor now supports Dynamic Avail Sizing, which reduces the slate viewers see when ad breaks, also called avails, in live HLS streams go unfilled. MediaTailor is a server-side ad insertion and channel assembly service that personalizes ads in live and on-demand video streams. When the ad decision server returns fewer ads than a break allows, dynamic avail sizing omits the unfilled time and resumes programming early instead of showing slate. To keep playback continuous, MediaTailor holds back a configurable reserve of content behind the live edge and draws on it when a break ends early. When the reserve runs low, MediaTailor requests extra ad time in later breaks to refill it. Free ad-supported streaming TV (FAST) channel operators can use dynamic avail sizing to keep viewers watching programming instead of filler content. Customers turn on dynamic avail sizing for each playback session by adding query parameters to the session initialization URL, with no change to their playback configuration. To learn more, see Dynamic avail sizing in the AWS Elemental MediaTailor User Guide.
title: AWS Elemental MediaTailor adds Dynamic Avail Sizing for live HLS

summary: The Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS) Linux broadcast SDK is now available for IVS Real-Time Streaming. Applications running on Linux can join an IVS stage, receive audio from participants, and send audio back to the stage in real time. The SDK provides a C API and Go language bindings. The Linux broadcast SDK is ideal for AI applications that enrich live streams by processing audio, such as transcription, translation, and content moderation, as well as voice agents that converse with participants. Amazon IVS is a managed live streaming solution designed to make low-latency or real-time video available to viewers around the world. Visit the AWS Region table for a full list of AWS Regions where the Amazon IVS console and APIs for control and creation of video streams are available. To learn more, see IVS Broadcast SDK: Linux Guide .
title: Amazon IVS Real-Time Streaming now provides a Linux broadcast SDK

summary: AWS Transform now puts applications at the center of every stage of the migration journey, so you can discover, plan, migrate, validate, and track the applications your business runs on rather than just the servers underneath them. Application-level grouping has been part of AWS rehost workflows for years, and AWS Transform now carries that same view through your entire migration. Enterprise migrations typically involve thousands of servers, but the questions that drive decisions are about applications. Using discovery data, AWS Transform identifies application boundaries and dependencies, then surfaces logical groupings of applications, each with its own total cost of ownership (TCO) and migration tracking. AWS Transform also adds built-in surveys, letting application owners validate ownership, system boundaries, and business criticality. A new migration dashboard keeps everyone aligned as the migration moves forward. It gives your team, partners, and leadership one current view of your applications, inventory, assessments, wave plans, and migration status. The dashboard pulls in data from every job in a workspace and updates as work progresses, so no one has to build or maintain separate status reports. You can customize the dashboard and ask questions about migration progress in chat. With a more connected workflow and improved visibility across the migration, AWS Transform lets you move to the cloud with more confidence. This capability is available in all AWS Regions whe
title: AWS Transform extends application-centric migration across the lifecycle

summary: AWS Transform for migrations now combines migration assessment and migration planning into a single migration job. Previously, you ran separate jobs to build a total cost of ownership (TCO) business case and to plan your migration. With this launch, you upload your on-premises inventory once and use it for both assessment and planning, in any order. After you upload your inventory data, you can estimate your AWS costs and build a business case, group your infrastructure into applications and plan migration waves, or do both. You can rerun either workflow as your data improves. For example, build a business case first and then plan waves from the same inventory, or plan your waves first and then estimate the cost of a single wave. Because assessment and planning share one inventory, your business case and migration plan stay consistent without moving data between jobs. After you finalize your plan and assessment, you can continue in the same job to migrate your networks, deploy landing zones, and migrate servers, storage, and containers. This newest release is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is offered . To learn more about migrating with AWS Transform, visit the product page and documentation .
title: AWS Transform combines migration assessment and planning in one experience

summary: Today, AWS announces deal-level revenue attribution for AWS Revenue Measurement (previously Partner Revenue Measurement) capabilities. AWS Partners can now see how the AWS revenue measured for their products maps to specific AWS Marketplace offers and/or APN Customer Engagements (ACE) opportunities. Until now, partners who implemented AWS Revenue Measurement via Resource Tagging , User Agent String or AWS Marketplace Metering could view aggregated, product-level attributed revenue. With this launch, partners can view attributed revenue by offers and opportunities on the Attributed Revenue dashboard in AWS Partner Central for components hosted in partners' own AWS accounts. Two new capabilities make this possible: Revenue Attribution IDs and Marketplace Revenue Share. A Revenue Attribution ID is a unique identifier that allows partners to allocate a product's measured AWS revenue to specific offers and opportunities. Partners create a Revenue Attribution ID, associate it with their deals, and enter a monthly attributed revenue allocation percentage for each deal. Partners with SaaS products on AWS Marketplace can automate allocation to offers with Marketplace Revenue Share. Each month, partners enter the percentage of the product's attributed revenue contributed by AWS Marketplace deals in the Revenue Attribution page, and AWS then calculates the attributed revenue for each active offer. Partners can use Revenue Attribution IDs alongside Marketplace Revenue Share to adjust a c
title: AWS Revenue Measurement now supports deal-level revenue attribution for AWS Marketplace offers and opportunities

summary: Amazon EMR Serverless now supports Flex execution, a new option that reduces the cost of non-urgent Spark batch jobs by up to 60% by running them on spare compute capacity. With Flex, you enable a single configuration when submitting a job, with no changes to Spark scripts or job definitions. Flex execution is designed for workloads that have flexible completion requirements, such as nightly batch ETL, backfill jobs, and development or testing pipelines. Start and execution times of Flex jobs vary because spare compute resources may not always be available immediately and may be reclaimed during execution. To reduce the likelihood and impact of interruptions, EMR Serverless spans availability zones, diversifies across instance types, places the Spark driver on dedicated capacity to protect job state, and retries interrupted tasks through Spark's built-in fault tolerance. You can also use Flex execution with Serverless Storage to offload shuffle data, adding another layer of resilience where retried tasks can resume from stored intermediate results instead of recomputing previous stages. Regardless of the execution option, Spark jobs on EMR Serverless have the same capabilities, including AWS Lake Formation fine-grained access control, AWS Graviton-based workers, and AWS Glue Data Catalog integration. Flex workers are billed at Flex rates for vCPU-hours and memory GB-hours, while the Spark driver and storage are billed at Standard rates. Amazon EMR Serverless Flex execution is
title: Amazon EMR Serverless introduces Flex execution

summary: AWS CloudFormation StackSets now shows stage-by-stage progress for deployments across accounts and AWS Regions, whether you target tens of accounts or thousands. You can follow each deployment as it progresses and take action when needed, without waiting for it to finish. StackSets lets you consistently apply the same infrastructure or application components, such as networking and security settings, across many accounts and Regions in one operation. With this launch, you can see how many stack instances are deployed, how many remain, and which ones need attention. This gives you confidence that a rollout is on track at every stage. Stage-level progress gives you a clear, detailed view of where each deployment stands. Previously, a StackSets deployment showed an overall status while it ran. Now, StackSets also reports progress for two stages. The first is role provisioning, which prepares access in each target account of a service-managed stack set. The second is stack deployment, which deploys your template as a stack instance in each account and Region. For example, in a deployment to 2,000 accounts in 3 Regions, you can see that role provisioning is complete and stack deployment has reached 40 percent, with 2,400 stack instances completed and 3,600 pending. Progress for each Region and the result of each stage remain available after the deployment completes. To get started, open the Progress view for a stack set operation in the CloudFormation console, or use the AWS CLI o
title: AWS CloudFormation StackSets adds progress visibility to simplify tracking deployments at scale

summary: Amazon S3 Tables replication now lets you make a read-only replica of your Apache Iceberg table a standalone, writable table with a single API call. S3 Tables replication keeps read-only replica tables in sync with your source tables across table buckets, AWS Regions, and accounts. Instead of copying a replica into a new table, you can promote it in place to move writes to another Region. When you disassociate a replica from replication, the standalone table keeps its namespace and table name, so your queries and pipeline code carry over when you point your applications at it. The promoted table then works like an S3 table you created, and you can use it as a source for new replicas. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where S3 Tables replication is supported. You can use the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or S3 Tables API. For pricing details, visit the Amazon S3 pricing page . To learn more, see the S3 Tables overview page and documentation .
title: Amazon S3 Tables now support promoting replicas to writable tables

summary: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. Organizations of every size, from startups to enterprises to public sector agencies, can now order Outposts racks connected to this newly supported Region to optimize for latency and data residency needs. This regional expansion provides additional flexibility in the number of AWS Regions that customers' Outposts can connect to. To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the AWS Outposts blog post and user guide . For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the AWS Outposts FAQs page . For pricing information in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region, please refer to this page .
title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region

summary: AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) now supports mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication for clients that present X.509 certificates. Until now, customers who needed mTLS with NLB built their own solutions or ran third-party proxies to authenticate clients. With this launch, NLB verifies client certificates on its TLS listeners, so only trusted clients can reach your targets. You can offload the compute-intensive processing required for mTLS authentication to NLB, without adding certificate logic to your backend applications. Mutual TLS is commonly used to secure communication between IoT devices, APIs, and microservices, and in regulated environments where both sides must prove their identity. To use mTLS, create a trust store with a certificate authority (CA) certificate bundle from a CA of your choice or AWS Private Certificate Authority, and attach it to a new or existing NLB TLS listener. To block certificates you no longer trust, add one or more certificate revocation lists (CRLs) to the trust store. To admit only specific clients, add client certificate filters that match the Common Name, Organizational Unit, or the DNS name or URI in the Subject Alternative Name, such as a SPIFFE ID. You can set up mTLS with the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), or APIs. Mutual TLS for NLB is available in all AWS commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where NLB is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Blog and the NLB User Guide.
title: AWS Network Load Balancer now supports mutual TLS authentication

summary: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges to help improve the security posture of your VPN tunnels. This feature supports your migration to post-quantum cryptography based on NIST guidelines. AWS Site-to-Site VPN is a fully managed service that creates an encrypted connection between your data center or branch office and your AWS resources using IPsec tunnels. With AWS Site-to-Site VPN, you can now configure post-quantum key exchange methods in your VPN tunnel options using the CreateVpnConnection and ModifyVpnTunnelOptions APIs. There is no additional charge for using post-quantum key exchanges. This capability is available in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where AWS Site-to-Site VPN is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Site-to-Site VPN documentation .
title: AWS Site-to-Site VPN now supports post-quantum key exchanges

summary: You can now associate AWS Network Firewall with NAT Gateway and use it both as an explicit proxy and a transparent firewall with native network address translation. You can use this capability with existing Network Firewall features to filter traffic to and from your applications and prevent data exfiltration and malware injection. AWS Network Firewall is a stateful, managed, network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention service for your VPC. Customers use it to filter their traffic and secure AWS resources. With this launch, you can configure Network Firewall with native NAT Gateway association and use it for both explicit proxy and routed filtering functionalities. Both these functionalities are governed by a single security policy that you maintain centrally. This capability works with existing Network Firewall features including managed rule groups from Amazon or Marketplace, active threat defense, Geo-IP filtering, URL and domain category filtering, container attribute-based rules for Amazon EKS and Amazon ECS, etc. You can access Network Firewall from any VPC in your environment, even the ones with overlapping IP CIDR space, using VPC endpoints. Your traffic reaches the firewall via the VPC endpoint and the filtered traffic exits directly from the NAT Gateway using its IP address. This capability is available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), US East (Ohio), US West (N. California), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Frankfurt), Asia Pacific
title: AWS Network Firewall launches explicit proxy functionality and NAT Gateway association

summary: Today, we are excited to announce the general availability of voice cloning in Amazon Polly, as a gated release. Using a few minutes of recordings from a consenting speaker, you can now create a cloned voice that sounds like that speaker. The cloned voices run on the Amazon Polly Generative engine, which delivers similar naturalness and accuracy as the rest of the generative voices. Voice cloning launches in seven languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Hindi. Each cloned voice speaks the language it was recorded in. The cloned voices are automatically encrypted and access-controlled: only you can access your cloned voices. Amazon Polly is a managed service that turns text into natural-sounding speech. With voice cloning, you can give your brand one recognizable voice across IVR and contact centers, voice agents, mobile apps, advertising, and connected devices. You can also create multiple voices for content creation use cases such as audiobooks, e-learning, podcasts, videos, and game characters. Amazon Polly does not retain a copy of your voice recordings once the voice is created and doesn't use them to train Polly models. Voice cloning is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Zurich), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). Voice cloning is already enabled for
title: Amazon Polly now supports voice cloning

summary: Today, AWS announces the Open Data and Interoperability category within the AWS Data Competency. The new category recognizes AWS Software Partners whose solutions keep customer data open and under customer control, letting multiple analytics engines and AI agents work on a single shared copy without moving or duplicating data. AI agents need current, governed data they can reach. According to Gartner, Inc., most organizations are prioritizing AI-ready data investments, yet many Chief Data and Analytics Officers report their current data architecture needs modernization. Partners in the Open Data and Interoperability category are validated for the following capabilities: - Open formats: Data stored in Apache Iceberg, readable by any tool. - Interoperable storage: One copy of data on AWS. - Bidirectional catalogs: Metadata synced through the Iceberg REST Catalog. - Interchangeable engines: Customers pick the right engine for each job. AWS Data Competency Partners also earn performance-based benefits including additional marketing and deal funding in 2027 and access to the AWS Data and AI Workshop. Customers now have a trusted way to find Software Partners whose solutions are built from the ground up for openness and interoperability, and those Partners gain a clear way to stand out. To learn more, read the APN Blog or visit the AWS Data Competency page .
title: AWS Data Competency adds Open Data and Interoperability category for Software Partners

summary: Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors the response time and GPU use of generative AI inference endpoints by default and notifies customers when responses slow down, GPUs sit mostly idle, or a configuration falls behind. Customers run GenAI Inference Recommendations to test configurations designed to restore response time or lower cost on their recent traffic, and they see measured results before anything changes in production. The best configuration for generative AI inference endpoints changes after deployment, as traffic shifts and new serving techniques become available. An endpoint whose latency rises or whose GPUs sit idle keeps running until users complain or the bill arrives. With this launch, SageMaker AI tracks response time and GPU capacity use and checks each endpoint's configuration. It does not read customer requests or responses. Findings include slower response times, unused GPU capacity, and configuration gaps such as an older serving container, missing speculative decoding, or missing GPU kernel tuning. When a change holds across the past week or a configuration gap is found, customers receive one AWS Health notification per endpoint in the AWS Management Console. Each notification links to the SageMaker AI Agentic Experience in SageMaker Studio with the endpoint and recent traffic already filled in. Customers run Generative AI Inference Recommendations, which compares the current configuration and options on response time, traffic handled, and cost per million to
title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects rising response times, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your generative AI inference endpoints

summary: AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) announces GetScopedCredentials, a new API that lets you scope down the permissions of existing temporary security credentials. With GetScopedCredentials, you can give your agents, sub agents and workloads their own set of credentials with only the permissions they need. You can call GetScopedCredentials with the temporary security credentials you already use to reduce permissions, session duration, or both. The resulting credentials preserve the caller's original identity, and permissions and session duration are monotonically narrowed so they never exceed those of the caller. Access to the API is controlled with IAM policies, and each call is logged to AWS CloudTrail for traceability. These capabilities make it easier to scope down permissions at runtime without changing how you manage identities. GetScopedCredentials is available in all AWS commercial Regions, AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Regions and China Regions. To get started, see the GetScopedCredentials API reference and Permissions for GetScopedCredentials .
title: AWS STS announces GetScopedCredentials to scope down permissions at runtime

summary: AWS announces the expansion of the Amazon Connect Customer Competency to Software Partners. The AWS Specialization now recognizes both Services and Software Partners with technical depth and proven success on Amazon Connect Customer—from migrating legacy contact centers and operationalizing AI at scale, to building new solutions on top of Amazon Connect Customer. Modern customers want smooth, tailored interactions wherever they engage, but legacy customer experience systems weren't designed to provide them. They rely on queues, manual routing, and handle-time metrics as control mechanisms, with AI added as a separate layer rather than built in from the start. The Competency adds three new categories for Software Partners: Customer Experience – Solution Extensions , for solutions that integrate with Amazon Connect Customer across the customer experience lifecycle; Connect A2A Collaboration – Agent Certification , for third-party AI agents certified to work alongside Amazon Connect Customer native AI agents during live customer contacts; and Connect Customer – Powered Partner Platform , for Partner-owned solutions that include Amazon Connect Customer as a core component. These join the two existing categories for Services Partners: Contact Center Transformation and AI-Powered Customer Experience. As the first AWS Competency directly aligned to an AWS service, it gives customers confidence they're working with Partners validated by AWS experts to deliver AI-native customer exper
title: AWS expands Amazon Connect Customer Competency to Software Partners

summary: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports PL/pgSQL, enabling developers to create and execute stored functions and procedures directly in the database. Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database designed for applications requiring active-active availability across multiple AWS Regions with fast reads and writes. You can now encapsulate procedural programming constructs such as IF/ELSE statements, loops, and variable assignments alongside SQL operations within the database. PL/pgSQL support reduces network round trips and improves application performance for data validation workflows, complex calculations, and transactional operations requiring multiple steps. Financial applications can implement account transfer procedures that validate balances, update multiple tables, and handle error conditions within a single database function. PL/pgSQL support is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available. To learn more, see PL/pgSQL in the Aurora DSQL User Guide.
title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now supports PL/pgSQL functions and procedures

summary: Today, AWS Marketplace announces the general availability of Data as a Service, a new product type that lets customers buy third-party datasets and licensed content. Customers often have the models and compute they need, but buying third-party data means adding each provider as a new supplier, negotiating separate contracts, and waiting on procurement cycles. Customers can now find and subscribe to Data as a Service products from AWS Marketplace sellers, and use them to enrich artificial intelligence (AI) applications, analytics, and other workloads. Customers purchase Data as a Service products through public or private offers, and charges appear on their existing AWS invoice. For example, an investment team evaluating private companies can connect its AI agents to private-market data through an API and to credit analysis through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Sellers set their own prices and license terms, using a contract, pay-as-you-go, or contract with consumption pricing model for each product. They can add a free trial to any of these models, or offer a product for free. They also define the onboarding and delivery experience, from setting up the customer's account to providing the data through an API, a web portal, a real-time feed, an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket, or another approach. To learn more, explore Data as a Service products on AWS Marketplace, the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide , and the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide .
title: Announcing Data as a Service for AWS Marketplace

summary: AWS License Manager now supports AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition) , so you can use your existing Microsoft Active Directory (AD) to manage user-based subscriptions for Microsoft Office, Visual Studio, and Remote Desktop Services Subscriber Access License (RDS SAL). Hybrid Edition, a feature of AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory, extends your existing directory into AWS. License Manager now works with that directory directly, so you no longer need to bear the cost of duplicating and maintaining the directory in AWS for licensing. Previously, onboarding Microsoft user-based subscriptions required a trust relationship between your directory and a second directory in AWS. If your security policies didn't allow that trust, you couldn't onboard without changing those policies. Now, license-included Microsoft Office and Visual Studio instances that you launch on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) join your existing directory and apply the same Group Policy settings, such as security baselines and audit policies, so you don't need to recreate them in a second directory. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where AWS License Manager user-based subscriptions and AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition) are available. To learn more, see the AWS License Manager User Guide , or get started in the AWS License Manager console .
title: AWS License Manager now supports AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition)

summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS Partner Central Agents now guide AWS Partners to create and enrich opportunities for a high-quality submission, and explain the assigned co-sell motion of each opportunity and why AWS assigned it. Since the launch of Agentic co-selling on June 16, 2026, AWS Partner Central Agents score every opportunity with an Opportunity Quality Score and assign co-sell motions including AWS Field-engaged, Agent-engaged, or Partner-led. When partners create an opportunity, the agents now guide them to a high-quality submission by asking for the details the Opportunity Quality Score measures, such as the customer's business problem, dated next steps, the Partner Primary Need from AWS, and the AWS services the customer will adopt, based on the co-selling best-practice guidance . After submission, the agents explain the reason behind each opportunity's co-sell motion and why AWS assigned it. Where the partner can act, the agents recommend the next step: for Agent-engaged opportunities, how to raise the Opportunity Quality Score; for Partner-led opportunities where AWS co-sell support was not requested, how to progress using agents. As partners act on these recommendations, the score and motion recalculate, and Agent-engaged opportunities move closer to AWS Field-engaged. The new enhanced experience is available today to AWS Partners in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. Partners can also use the agentic experience in native AI tools like AWS Quick and Kiro, or thro
title: AWS Partner Central Agents now guide higher-quality co-sell submissions and explain co-sell motions

summary: Today, AWS announces that AWS Partner Central Agents can now generate Value Realization Plans (VRPs) for the Business Value Realization (BVR) motion in AWS Partner Central . The VRP is the plan of record for a BVR engagement. The agentic experience generates a VRP that includes the customer's business goals; plan for adoption, change management, and governance; and baseline key performance indicators (KPIs) for Partners to review and finalize. AWS Partner Central launched the BVR motion on June 16, 2026, to help Partners drive business outcomes for their customers by structuring AWS service adoption into defined stages, with funding tied to demonstrated value. With this launch, Partners in the BVR motion no longer start a VRP from a blank page. The agents recommend KPIs, ramp targets, and baseline measurements based on nomination data, opportunity context, and service benchmarks. They also flag gaps before submission, such as a lack of customer sponsorship, and identify next steps. Partners start from a complete draft and refine it with their customer. BVR is available in AWS Partner Central for consulting, system integrator, and managed services partners with Advanced or Premier tier status and a qualifying domain competency. This capability is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. To get started, partners sign in to AWS Partner Central and choose Funding benefits, Business Value Realization. After AWS approves a nomination, partners ask AWS Partner Central Agents,
title: AWS Partner Central Agents now generate Value Realization Plans

summary: Today, AWS announces AWS Marketplace Express Checkout , a simpler way for businesses that don't have an existing AWS account to buy software from established vendors in AWS Marketplace . Express Checkout is built for businesses that don't use AWS today and just want to buy software. With no cloud setup required, buyers sign in with an email address or a social login, pay with a credit or debit card, and check out in a few steps. Businesses that buy multiple applications this way can manage all of their Express Checkout subscriptions in one place, without a separate billing login for each vendor. From there, they can update their card, download invoices, or cancel a subscription themselves. For sellers, Express Checkout opens a new segment of self-serve business buyers, using the same listing and AWS Marketplace integration they use today. Sellers with an eligible public SaaS listing can request to add their product to the Express Checkout catalog. Express Checkout is available for eligible SaaS products to buyers in the United States and Canada. Businesses that already use AWS can continue to buy in AWS Marketplace with their AWS account. To get started, visit the AWS Marketplace Express Checkout page . To learn more, see the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide and the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide .
title: AWS Marketplace now offers Express Checkout for buyers without an AWS account

summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports private certificate authorities (CAs) for custom OAuth 2.0 credential providers. If you already connect your agents to identity providers (IdPs) hosted in your VPC, you can now configure those connections to trust certificates issued by your own CA — including AWS Private CA, enterprise CAs, and self-signed root CAs. AgentCore Identity has supported private IdP connectivity through Amazon VPC Lattice, but until now the IdP still had to present a publicly trusted TLS certificate over that private connection. With private CA support, you store your CA certificate in AWS Secrets Manager or Amazon S3 and reference it from your credential provider configuration. AgentCore Identity uses it to verify the IdP's server certificate directly, removing the need for a publicly trusted certificate or additional infrastructure on the private network path. You can rotate the CA certificate without downtime by combining the current and new certificates in a single PEM file, and remove private CA trust by updating the credential provider without the certificate reference. Private CA support for AgentCore Identity is available in all AWS Regions where AgentCore Identity supports private IdP connectivity. To get started, see Connect to private identity providers in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide. To learn more, visit the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore product page .
title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity adds private certificate authority support

summary: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth dynamic client registration (DCR, RFC 7591). Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes.
