With DCR support, Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and AI agents can register themselves at runtime. Previously, you had to create an application client in advance for each AI client before it could connect to an MCP server that uses Cognito for authorization. With DCR, Cognito advertises a registration endpoint in its OAuth authorization server metadata. MCP clients that support dynamic client registration discover the endpoint, register to receive a client ID, and then sign users in. You control who can register: either require registration requests to present an access token with a registration scope, or turn on open registration so that any client can register. Dynamically registered clients appear with your other app clients with a client ID prefix and a client type you can filter on, so you can manage them with the same console and APIs. DCR is available on the Essentials and Plus feature plans in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available. To learn more, see Dynamic client registration in the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide.
title: Amazon Cognito now supports dynamic client registration

summary: Amazon VPC Flow Logs now adds Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) metadata to flow log records. Each record identifies the pod that sent or received the traffic, along with its cluster, namespace and labels. This makes it faster to investigate security events, understand traffic patterns, and troubleshoot network issues in your EKS clusters, without running monitoring software on your nodes. Amazon EKS runs pods on Amazon EC2 instances, called nodes, and many pods can share one node's network interfaces. Previously, flow log records showed the network interface and IP address for each flow, not the pod behind it. Pods are short-lived, so by the time you investigated unexpected traffic, that IP address could belong to a different pod. To trace traffic back to the right pod, teams built custom tools or ran monitoring software on every node. Now, each record names the pod that sent or received the traffic, so one log gives you both VPC and Kubernetes context. For example, if a pod sends unexpected traffic to a database in your VPC, the record shows the pod and its namespace, even after that pod is replaced. To get started, create a flow log for your cluster's VPC or subnets, and add the EKS fields to the log format. You don't need to change your cluster or applications. The fields are available for pods on Amazon EC2 instances, including EKS Auto Mode, managed node groups and self-managed nodes, that use the Amazon VPC CNI plugin for Kubernetes. Logs go to the same de
title: Amazon VPC Flow Logs now supports Amazon EKS metadata

summary: Amazon Connect Customer now provides agents with a generative AI-powered post-contact summary of each chat conversation inside the Contact Control Panel (CCP) within seconds after the chat ends, so agents can complete after contact work from the summary instead of rereading the transcript. The summary covers what the customer needed, the actions the agent took, and any open items, and it appears at the end of the chat transcript. Conversational analytics already generates these summaries for voice and email contacts in the CCP, and this launch adds chat. An airline agent who finishes a flight rebooking chat sees the new travel date, the fare difference charged, and the confirmation sent, then writes the wrap-up note from those three facts. Summaries follow your flow's redaction settings and use the same security profile permissions as voice summaries, so administrators who already enabled voice summaries can turn on chat analytics with post-contact summary in the Set recording and analytics behavior block. To learn more, see View generative AI-powered post-contact summaries in Connect Customer .
title: Amazon Connect Customer now provides AI chat summaries in the CCP

summary: Amazon Inspector Code Security now supports GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) integration and private network connectivity for GHES and GitLab Self-Managed. Code Security is also launching automatic fix pull requests in public preview. Organizations that host GHES or GitLab Self-Managed in private networks can now connect through Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) configurations or AWS CodeConnections, so they can scan repositories without opening their firewalls to the entire AWS IP address range. Amazon Inspector Code Security scans first-party application source code, third-party dependencies, and Infrastructure as Code for vulnerabilities in repositories on GitHub, GHES, and GitLab Self-Managed. With automatic fix pull requests, Amazon Inspector turns its suggested fix into a pull request that developers review and choose whether to merge, instead of applying the fix by hand. It opens pull requests only for high-confidence fixes to static application security testing (SAST) findings at or above a severity you set. These features are available in all 10 AWS Regions where Amazon Inspector Code Security is available: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Singapore). To learn more, see the Amazon Inspector User Guide and the Amazon Inspector product page .
title: Amazon Inspector Code Security adds GitHub Enterprise Server and private connectivity

summary: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing (formerly AWS Security Agent) now lets you pause a running penetration test job and resume it later from its last saved checkpoint. Continuum for Penetration Testing runs on-demand, AI-driven penetration tests against your web applications and APIs. Previously, a pen test job that failed due to client configuration error could not continue, so security teams had to start a new pen test job and repeat work the agent had already done. When you resume a paused or failed pen test job, it keeps its findings and completed work and continues where it left off. You can pause a pen test job during a deployment or maintenance window, raise the task-hour limit of a pen test job that has reached it, or replace test credentials that expired mid-test. Before you resume, you can also update the network traffic settings or VPC configuration, while the pen test job's scope, including its target endpoints, stays the same. You can pause and resume pen test jobs in the web application or with the StopPentestJob and ResumePentestJob APIs. You can resume a pen test job within 7 days of its creation. Pause and resume is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing is available. To learn more, visit our documentation page .
title: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing now supports pause and resume

summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances now support nested virtualization, so your agents can run their own virtual machines and emulators inside a session with Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM). Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. Nested virtualization serves agents that rely on tools that run in a virtual machine, such as mobile emulators or virtual machine sandboxes. You turn on nested virtualization when you create a Linux capacity provider, and agents in every session on its instances can use KVM. For example, your agents can run Android emulators to build and test mobile apps, or start lightweight virtual machines to isolate the code that they run. Nested virtualization works on supported Intel-based instance types, including the C7i, C8i, M7i, M8i, R7i, and R8i families. Nested virtualization is available on supported instance types in all AWS Regions where AgentCore runtime instances are available. To get started, see the following resources: Run virtual machines in agents on runtime instances in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide AgentCore pricing
title: AgentCore runtime instances now support Nested Virtualization

summary: Aurora PostgreSQL and Aurora MySQL clusters can now move from one Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to another without data migration. You can move a cluster with a single API call or a modify action in the Amazon RDS console. This lets you move a cluster to a VPC with more IP address space or a non-overlapping CIDR range, consolidate your network architecture, or meet changing security and compliance requirements. Previously, moving an Aurora cluster to a different VPC meant creating a new cluster in the target VPC, migrating your data, and updating your applications with new connection strings. Now, a single ModifyDBCluster API call moves your existing cluster to the new VPC. Your data stays in place, your cluster endpoint stays the same, and connectivity is interrupted only briefly during the move. Before you start, turn off features that are tied to the cluster's current VPC, such as Aurora Global Database, Amazon RDS Proxy, and Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments. You can set them up again in the new VPC after the move. This feature is available for Aurora PostgreSQL and Aurora MySQL in all AWS Regions where Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration is available. To get started, use the Amazon RDS console , AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. To learn more, see the Aurora User Guide .
title: Amazon Aurora now supports moving clusters to a different VPC

summary: Aurora PostgreSQL databases created with express configuration can now move into an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with a single API call or a modify action in the Amazon RDS console. This helps you take AI-built prototypes and other applications to production without migrating data, while meeting your security and compliance requirements. You can also create a new database cluster inside a VPC using express configuration. With express configuration, Aurora PostgreSQL lets you create and query a serverless database in seconds. Connectivity runs through an internet access gateway, which makes this a good fit for rapid prototyping and AI agent-driven development. When your application is ready for production, a single ModifyDBCluster API call moves the cluster into a VPC and turns off the internet access gateway. That gives you security groups, private subnets, and features such as Aurora Global Database, Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, and Amazon RDS Proxy. The move requires no data migration, keeps your cluster endpoint the same, and interrupts connectivity only briefly. You can also reverse it with the same API call. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration is available. To get started, use the Amazon RDS console , AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. To learn more, see the Aurora User Guide .
title: Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration now supports Amazon VPC

summary: Amazon Cognito now integrates with AWS Secrets Manager , so you can store and manage your user pool app client secrets in Secrets Manager. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. An app client secret authenticates your application to Cognito. Previously, you had to manage and rotate these secrets in Cognito directly. With this integration, you can leverage Secrets Manager for capabilities including rotation, access control with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies, and encryption with an AWS managed key or your own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. This can help with periodic credential rotation or compliance requirements; this also helps with keeping secrets out of the console. You can enable this integration for either a new or an existing app client, and disable it at any time. This integration is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito and AWS Secrets Manager are available, except AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany). Standard AWS Secrets Manager charges apply. To learn more, see the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide for instructions.
title: Amazon Cognito now supports AWS Secrets Manager for app client secrets

summary: AWS WAF now gives you one place to find and stop unwanted traffic across every application in your account. The new AWS WAF security analytics dashboard brings together traffic from all of your protection packs (web ACLs), whether they protect Regional resources or Amazon CloudFront distributions, into a single view. The dashboard also lets you search request logs right in the console, with no logging pipeline to build, and includes 21 days of full-fidelity request data at no additional cost. It is available alongside the existing dashboard for each protection pack (WebACL), which continues to work as it does today. Until now, spotting a trend across your applications, such as a bot campaign hitting several endpoints or a spike in blocked requests, meant opening each web ACL in turn or individually querying AWS WAF logs. With the AWS WAF security analytics dashboard, you can analyze traffic data from every protection pack (WebACL) at once. You can filter and group traffic by dimensions such as client IP address, country, ASN, user agent, JA4 fingerprint, host, path, rule triggered, and labels. You can see which endpoints are affected and how traffic is changing across all of them. The data is full-fidelity rather than sampled, and filters apply across the whole dashboard. Investigating individual requests has also required delivering AWS WAF logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Amazon Data Firehose and writing queries. AWS WAF Security analytics dashboard includes a
title: AWS WAF launches new Security Analytics Dashboard for real-time investigations

summary: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute function timeout for Event Functions that run on demand, doubling the 15-minute limit for synchronous , asynchronous , and event source mapping (ESM) invocations. On Lambda Managed Instances , synchronous invocations also support up to 30 minutes, while asynchronous and ESM invocations keep the 90-minute timeout launched in September 2026. You can now run long-running workloads such as AI inference, media transcoding, and financial calculations for spiky or steady-state traffic without re-architecting your applications. Customers use Event Functions to build event-driven processors, API backends, and data pipelines. By default, Event Functions run on demand, and Lambda scales them automatically to handle spiky traffic. For steady-state traffic, you can also run them on Lambda Managed Instances, which runs functions on Amazon EC2 instances and maintains the operational simplicity of Lambda. For data-intensive workloads such as AI inference and media processing that run on demand and need longer continuous execution, the 15-minute function timeout had required customers to adopt architectural workarounds. With today's launch, these workloads can run for up to 30 minutes, including when you use Lambda durable functions or invoke your functions from AWS Step Functions Standard workflows . For Event Functions that run on demand, the 30-minute timeout is available in all commercial AWS Regions . On Lambda Managed Instances, it is available for sy
title: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute timeout for on-demand Event Functions

summary: Amazon Route 53 now offers Private Endpoint Health Checks, enabling business-critical workloads that never touch the public internet, such as internal APIs, databases, and self-hosted nodes behind internal load balancers or in private subnets, to use native health monitoring and automatic DNS failover. Customers can health-check any reachable private target by IP address, domain, or port over HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP. Customers can associate these health checks with Route 53 DNS records across routing policies in private hosted zones, so Route 53 routes traffic only to healthy endpoints and manages failover automatically. Previously, teams built custom control loops using Amazon CloudWatch alarms, AWS Lambda functions, and the Route 53 API to achieve DNS failover for private resources. With t his approach , failover took several minutes and added operational burden. Detection and DNS failover with Private Endpoint Health Checks are designed to complete in seconds rather than minutes, the service is fully managed, and nothing is exposed to the public internet. The feature supports on-premises and hybrid endpoints reachable from the VPC over AWS Direct Connect or AWS Site-to-Site VPN, enabling resilience patterns such as active-passive disaster recovery and cross-Region DR over AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN. Amazon Route 53 Private Endpoint Health Checks is available today in all AWS commercial regions. To learn more, visit the Amazon Route 53 Developer Guide and the Route 53
title: Amazon Route 53 now supports health checks for private endpoints

summary: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications now supports WebAuthn redirection, so users can sign in to websites and applications in their streaming session with a FIDO2 authenticator on their local device, such as a security key, Windows Hello, or Touch ID. Previously, an authenticator attached to the user's computer was not available inside the streaming session, so organizations that require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) had to use weaker sign-in methods or keep those applications off WorkSpaces Applications. This helps organizations with FIDO2 requirements stream those applications. When an application in the session makes a WebAuthn request, WorkSpaces Applications forwards it to the user's device, where the authenticator signs it and returns the response. Private keys never leave the user's device. Administrators turn it on per stack in the console or API, and on Windows fleets can limit it to an allow list of processes. For example, a bank can let employees sign in to Microsoft 365 in their streaming session with the same security key they use on their laptop. WebAuthn redirection is available at no additional charge in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where WorkSpaces Applications is available. To get started, select Enable WebAuthn redirection under User Settings for your stack, use an image with the WorkSpaces Applications agent released on or after October 20, 2026, and connect with the WorkSpaces Applications client for Windows (1.
title: Amazon WorkSpaces Applications now supports WebAuthn redirection

summary: AWS Lambda announces OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for Lambda durable functions. You can now trace your durable executions and emit traces to Amazon CloudWatch and other industry-standard observability tools. This helps you find bottlenecks in your system, root cause failures faster, and understand how your workflows behave in production. With Lambda durable functions, you can build resilient, multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing and automatic retries. Durable functions can run for hours, or days, suspending and resuming across many Lambda invocations. The new OpenTelemetry plugin emits a unified trace that spans a full durable execution, including steps, waits, callbacks, and chained function invocations. You can use the trace to gain operational insights across your executions including step durations, retries, and failures across executions. The OpenTelemetry plugin is available for the TypeScript, Python, and Java SDKs. You can enable OpenTelemetry support by adding the OpenTelemetry plugin package alongside the Durable Execution SDK and register it on your durable handler or using an environment variable. OpenTelemetry support for Lambda durable functions is available in all AWS Regions that support Lambda durable functions. To get started, see the OpenTelemetry plugin documentation , the plugin interface documentation , and the sample application . To learn more, read the blog post .
title: AWS Lambda durable functions now supports OpenTelemetry tracing

summary: You can now assess a seller's security, buy, and deploy supported products in one conversation with AWS Marketplace agent mode, the conversational AI experience for procuring cloud solutions. You share your requirement once, and agent mode applies them as it guides you through discovery, purchase, and deployment. Describe your use case in natural language to get recommended software, services, AI agents and tools, and multi-product solutions that fit your business needs. To assess a seller's security, request documents such as System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 reports, and get a criterion-by-criterion assessment against a standard cloud security questionnaire, the Consensus Assessments Initiative Questionnaire (CAIQ). When you're ready to buy, sign in with your AWS account. Agent mode explains pricing and terms so you know what you're committing to, shows your organizations' purchase requirements, and completes the purchase after you review the terms and confirm. For supported products, agent mode reviews your AWS environment, proposes a deployment plan with the estimated monthly cost, and deploys after you approve. It then shows you how to start using the product and helps you troubleshoot if a step fails. Agent mode is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available. To get started, open agent mode on the AWS Marketplace website. To learn more, see Agent mode for AWS Marketplace in the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide.
title: AWS Marketplace agent mode now helps you assess, buy, and deploy solutions

summary: Amazon Connect Customer announces the general availability of Resolutions, an agentic operations solution that resolves high-volume work end-to-end, including refund requests, transaction disputes, fraud investigations, and insurance claims. Resolutions helps businesses reduce resolution times and cost to serve by combining the reasoning of AI agents with the reliability of deterministic workflows. Every request follows business policy, gets the oversight it requires, and ends in a verifiable outcome. Managers describe a process in natural language or upload standard operating procedures (SOPs), and Resolutions generates a Work plan in minutes. As it builds the Work plan, Resolutions asks clarifying questions that surface exceptions, set decision rules, and define approval thresholds, closing the gaps an SOP leaves open. Resolutions then opens a Resolutions Case for each incoming request and applies the right Work plan. AI agents gather information, apply policy, act across your business applications, and ask customers for missing details to drive every Case to completion. Each Step can run on prebuilt AI agents, AI agents configured in Amazon Connect Customer, or your own, while human specialists handle approvals and exceptions with the context they need to act. For example, a bank resolving a transaction dispute can have AI agents pull the transaction history, check the claim against chargeback rules, email the cardholder for a missing receipt, and issue a provisional credi
title: Amazon Connect launches Resolutions, an agentic solution for high-volume operational work

summary: Amazon CloudFront now lets web development platforms and SaaS providers move a customer's domain to their platform in a single request with no downtime, and serve requests to the domain while the TLS certificate is being configured. The CloudFront multi-tenant distributions allow these platforms to serve many customer domains from one shared configuration. Together, these features help move existing AWS customers to multi-tenant distributions without impacting their traffic. Previously, moving a domain that was already in use required disabling the original distribution, using a wildcard workaround, or contacting AWS Support. Now you can bring customer domains onto your multi-tenant setup as part of creating or updating a tenant. With the new OnDomainTakeover option, CloudFront checks domain ownership through DNS records and then moves one or more domains in a single request. This works within an AWS account or across accounts. If you add a domain before its certificate is issued, CloudFront serves it over HTTP until you attach a certificate. That gives you time to validate the domain with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) or another certificate authority and attach the certificate once it's issued. These features are available in all edge locations at no additional cost. To learn more, see Move domains and Domains without a certificate in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide.
title: Amazon CloudFront simplifies domain moves and onboarding for SaaS Manager

summary: Amazon CloudFront now allows web development and SaaS platforms to serve different tiers of customers on the same wildcard domain by using IP addresses to route them to the right configuration. For example, these platforms can serve premium and pro customers from dedicated Anycast static IP address lists, each with its own configuration, and serve free-tier customers on the shared CloudFront IP addresses, all under *. example.com . Additionally, these customers also have visibility into viewer connections with connection logging. Previously, CloudFront chose the configuration from the domain name alone, so the same domain always went to the same configuration. With address-based selection, you can register the same wildcard domain on several IP lists and send each list to its own tenant. Because you control which clients resolve to which IP list, you can shift traffic between your service tiers without your customers needing to make any changes. You can also serve IoT devices, embedded SDKs, and older TLS clients that connect by IP address without sending a domain name in the TLS handshake (Server Name Indication, or SNI). With viewer fallback, you choose a distribution to accept these connections, and CloudFront uses the Host header in each request to serve the right content. Connection logs now also record HTTPS connections to these tenants which helps you troubleshoot how clients connect. These features are available at all CloudFront edge locations. To learn more, see Add
title: Amazon CloudFront adds IP based routing and connection logs to SaaS Manager

summary: With upgrades to its storage layer, Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput for many transactional workloads. Data loads finish sooner, and tables whose primary key always increases, such as tables keyed by a timestamp, an identity column, or a time-ordered ID like ULID or UUIDv7, see even greater benefits. Applications such as audit logs, ledgers, and event feeds are read in time order, and keying them by time keeps those reads fast. You can now use that design for write-heavy tables too. In our tests, an audit log table keyed by event time accepted up to 200% more inserts per second. The improvement is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora DSQL is available, for new and existing clusters, at no additional cost. To learn more, see the Aurora DSQL User Guide .
title: Amazon Aurora DSQL now delivers up to 50% higher write throughput

summary: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth client ID metadata documents (CIMD). Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. With CIMD, Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and AI agents can sign users in to your user pool without registering a separate app client. Previously, each external client needed its own app client, either created in advance or through dynamic client registration, and you had to manage and clean up those clients over time. With CIMD, a client uses an HTTPS URL as its client ID and publishes a JSON metadata document at that URL. When the client starts sign-in, Cognito fetches and validates the document and uses it to identify the client and validate its sign-in request. You decide which clients to accept with CIMD policies that map URL patterns to one of your app clients, and Cognito grants only the scopes and grant types that both the app client and the metadata document allow. For example, a company that runs an MCP server can accept an AI assistant by allowing the URL where that assistant publishes its metadata without creating or maintaining an app client for it. CIMD is available on the Essentials and Plus feature plans in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available. To learn more, see Client ID metadata documents (CIMD) in the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide.
title: Amazon Cognito now supports client ID metadata documents

summary: AWS Marketplace now supports agentic payments over the x402 protocol, so AI agents can discover and buy select products and pay per request in US dollars through AgentCore payments, part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Agents often need paid APIs, data, or content mid-task, but access usually requires a person to sign up, add a payment method, and create an API key. With agentic payments, customers skip that per-seller setup, and charges settle on their existing AWS bill with no crypto wallet required. Customers enable the AWS Marketplace payment connector in AgentCore payments, then they or their agents find listings through the AWS Marketplace connector in AgentCore Gateway. For example, a research agent can buy a single web search, or a coding agent can call a paid guardrail service. Customers can set spending limits, approved sellers, and guardrails before agents transact, Private Marketplace policies still apply, and transactions appear in AWS CloudTrail and AWS Cost Explorer. AWS Marketplace sellers can charge AI agents per request without building a sign-up flow or billing system. They register with AWS Marketplace, configure agentic payments for their listings, and integrate the AWS Marketplace x402 SDK . AWS Marketplace collects customer payments and pays sellers through their AWS Marketplace seller disbursements, like other AWS Marketplace transactions. The capability is available in all AWS Regions where AgentCore payments is available. To learn more, see AWS Marketpl
title: AWS Marketplace now supports agentic payments with AgentCore

summary: AWS RTB Fabric Modules from AdTech partners including Pixalate, WURFL by ScientiaMobile, and Picnic are now available through AWS Marketplace. With AWS RTB Fabric Modules, any demand-side platform (DSP), supply-side platform (SSP), and publisher on RTB Fabric can discover, configure, and deploy partner modules for use cases such as brand safety, fraud detection, device detection, and inventory quality directly in their real-time bidding workloads. Modules run inline at single-digit millisecond performance, with no custom integration, and partner charges appear on your single AWS bill. To optimize advertising revenue, AdTech companies rely on partner signals to increase bid rates. Previously, each new partner required a custom integration that could take weeks to months, its own contract and procurement cycle, and added latency to the bid path. Now, DSPs, SSPs, and publishers can find modules in AWS Marketplace and attach them to RTB Fabric in minutes. Modules filter, enrich, or observe bid requests before they reach the bidder, to improve bid performance and effectiveness without needing to make any code changes. At launch, modules are available from AdTech partners including Pixalate for invalid traffic filtering (IVT) and screening, WURFL by ScientiaMobile for device detection and contextual signals, and Picnic for inventory quality. For third-party AdTech module providers, they can now more easily reach AWS RTB Fabric customers from a single AWS Marketplace listing. AWS RT
title: AWS RTB Fabric Modules are now generally available through AWS Marketplace

summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of a new Local Zone in Bogotá, Colombia, bringing AWS infrastructure closer to end users for applications that require single-digit millisecond latency. You can use the Bogotá Local Zone for workloads such as real-time gaming, live video streaming, medical imaging, and financial transaction processing. AWS Local Zones are infrastructure deployments that place compute, storage, networking, and other select AWS services closer to metropolitan areas, with the same APIs and tools as AWS Regions. You pay only for what you use, with no minimum commitment. Pricing options include On-Demand, Savings Plans, and Spot Instances. AWS Local Zones are available in more than 30 locations worldwide. The AWS Local Zone in Bogotá supports Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) with C7i, M7i, and R7i instances, Amazon S3 with the One Zone-Infrequent Access storage class, Amazon EBS with local snapshots and volume types gp3, gp2, and io1, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC), AWS Direct Connect, and Application Load Balancer. To get started, enable the AWS Local Zone in Bogotá (us-east-1-bog-1a) from the Regions and Zones tab in the AWS Global View or by using the ModifyAvailabilityZoneGroup API. For pricing information, visit the AWS Local Zones pricing page . To learn more, visit the AWS Local Zones overview page .
title: Announcing the general availability of a new AWS Local Zone in Bogotá, Colombia

summary: Amazon VPC Lattice now publishes Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VPC resources. Resource owners — those who share resources via VPC Lattice — and resource consumers — those who access those shared resources — can now see TCP traffic to resources such as databases, clusters, and on-premises endpoints. Resource owners get metrics for resource gateways and resource configurations. Consumers get metrics for resource endpoints, service network endpoints, and service network VPC associations. Previously, resource access logs were the primary way to see this traffic, but they required additional processing and provided limited real-time visibility. Now you can monitor your layer-4 resources directly in CloudWatch. With these metrics, you can proactively catch connectivity issues and optimize resource capacity. Capacity planning metrics — including bytes processed, new flows, and active flows — let resource owners monitor traffic per resource gateway and per resource configuration to track load on shared resources. Reliability metrics, such as dropped packets, help you detect problems early. Resource gateways also report port allocation errors, which show when a resource gateway needs more IPv4 addresses per network interface. Consumers can monitor traffic per resource endpoint, service network endpoint, or service network VPC association. They can set CloudWatch alarms for when new flows drop to zero or dropped packets increase, catching an unreachable resource before their applicatio
title: Amazon VPC Lattice now supports CloudWatch metrics for VPC resources

summary: AWS Data Exports for Cost and Usage Report (CUR) 2.0 now includes standardized cost and rate columns that represent cost consistently across AWS purchase options, including On Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, EC2 Spot, and EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML. These 14 columns are added when you enable Include Standardized cost and rate columns while setting up a new CUR 2.0 export or editing an existing CUR 2.0 and these columns have the prefix cost_analytics_. With these new columns, you can quantify the savings you realize from commitments, discounts, and tiered pricing, and analyze amortized cost the same way for every pricing model with multiple payment options, directly in CUR 2.0. Previously, calculating savings required combining CUR with Savings Plans rates and public price lists, and amortized cost used different columns for each pricing model. Now each line item carries billed, effective, list, contracted, public on-demand cost, the public equivalent of billed and effective cost before discounts, and a rate for each, so you can measure savings and amortized cost without building your own calculations. To add the columns, select Include standardized cost and rate columns when you create or edit a CUR 2.0 export. In Cost Explorer, choose the new cost types under Advanced options to see the same costs. Standardized cost and rate columns are available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, s
title: AWS launches standardized cost and rate columns in CUR 2.0 and Cost Explorer

summary: AWS is announcing the general availability of new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T9g instances, which offer the best price performance among general-purpose EC2 instances. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors and built on the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. T9g instances deliver up to 45% better price performance compared to previous generation T4g instances, and offer four sizes: nano, micro, small, and medium. These instances are designed for workloads requiring low to moderate CPU utilization, including data processing, login gateways, small databases, microservices, low-traffic websites, freemium services, staging and development, and short-duration compute tasks such as batch processing, event-driven functions, and CI/CD pipelines. T9g instances deliver up to 2.3x the compute performance, 1.5x higher network bandwidth, and 2.8x higher EBS bandwidth compared to T4g instances. They are built on the sixth-generation AWS Nitro System and feature the Nitro Isolation Engine, harnessing formal verification to provide mathematical assurance that customer workloads are isolated from each other and AWS operators, pioneering a new standard for mathematically proven cloud security. T9g instances use the same CPU credit system as T4g with Standard and Unlimited modes, so existing T customers can upgrade to T9g and immediately benefit from better price performance, enabling them to lower their TCO. For customers new to AWS or migrating from on-premises, T9g
title: Introducing Amazon EC2 T9g instances based on Graviton5

summary: Today, AWS announced the general availability of .NET 11 support in AWS Transform for .NET. Support for VB.NET, desktop projects, and mobile projects, previously in preview, is also now generally available. You can modernize a broad range of Windows .NET workloads to the latest version of .NET and lower costs by running them on Linux. Modernized workloads gain the performance improvements, new C# language features, and improved diagnostics in .NET 11. AWS Transform modernizes both legacy .NET Framework applications (version 3.5 and later) and modern .NET applications (versions 5 through 10) to .NET 11. It transforms code written in C# and VB.NET. Supported project types include class libraries, console applications, ASP.NET web projects (MVC, Web API, and Web Forms), web services (ASMX and WCF), desktop applications (WinForms and WPF), mobile applications (Xamarin), unit test projects (MSTest, NUnit, and xUnit), and Windows services. You can run all transformed applications except desktop and mobile projects on Linux, which can reduce operating costs by up to 40%. This capability is available at no additional cost in all eight AWS Regions where AWS Transform is offered: US East (N. Virginia), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more, see Modernizing .NET with AWS Transform in the AWS Transform User Guide.
title: AWS Transform announces support for .NET 11 and expanded project types

summary: You can now upgrade existing Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters from Standard brokers to Express brokers in place, with fully managed data migration and no application changes. Express brokers are designed to deliver up to 3x more throughput per broker, scale up to 20x faster, and recover up to 90% faster compared to Standard brokers. With in-place upgrade, you can get the performance and operational benefits of Express brokers in hours, without needing to create a new cluster or having to migrate your data and applications to it. The upgrade keeps cluster endpoints unchanged, eliminating application cutovers, and preserves consumer offsets, so stateful applications such as Apache Flink and Kafka Streams continue without reprocessing or duplicates. Express brokers make Apache Kafka simpler to manage and more cost-effective to run at scale, with pay-as-you-go storage that scales automatically and built-in best practice defaults for higher resilience. Previously, upgrading to Express brokers meant creating a new cluster and migrating workloads to it, which required careful planning and cross-team coordination. With this launch, you can upgrade your existing Standard brokers to Express brokers in-place, without interrupting your applications, while maintaining complete control over the upgrade process. The upgrade adds Express brokers to your cluster and moves your topics to them, either automatically or in batches you control. Your Standard brokers stay in the cluster until you ch
title: Amazon MSK now supports in-place upgrade from Standard brokers to Express brokers

summary: Today, AWS announced the general availability of third-party UI component porting for ASP.NET web site modernization in AWS Transform. When AWS Transform modernizes a legacy ASP.NET web site, it now detects dependencies on popular third-party UI component libraries. You can replace them with license-free Microsoft-native and open-source components, or you can keep using vendor UI libraries. AWS Transform rewrites legacy ASP.NET web sites for ASP.NET Core UI frameworks. When the AWS Transform for .NET modernization agent finds a dependency on a popular third-party UI library, it offers two options. The first option is for customers who require open-source software only. The agent replaces each proprietary control with a Microsoft-native or open-source control on the target UI framework and removes the original dependency. The second option is for customers who want to keep using vendor libraries. The agent adds code comments and next-step instructions for moving to an equivalent vendor library on the target UI framework. You then arrange licensing with the vendor and finish the port using an AI coding companion. This capability is available at no additional cost in all eight AWS Regions where AWS Transform is offered: US East (N. Virginia), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more, see Porting UI layer code in the AWS Transform User Guide.
title: AWS Transform announces UI component modernization for Windows web applications

summary: Amazon Connect Customer enhances service level agreements (SLAs) for cases, so teams can set service goals for more of their work and respond faster when a case falls behind. Admins can set SLAs on case fields beyond status, such as requiring a case’s severity to drop from high to medium within 24 hours. Admins can add an email action to SLA breach rules, so the assigned agent learns right away when a case misses its SLA. Developers can use APIs to adjust a case’s SLA deadline when the team is waiting on information from an outside party, such as a partner. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .
title: Amazon Connect Customer expands how teams track and act on service level agreements for cases

summary: Starting today, Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition 8.4 supports MySQL 8.4.12. This release includes several security enhancements and bug fixes. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by community MySQL. For more details, refer to the Aurora MySQL 8.4 and MySQL 8.4.12 release notes. You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your clusters in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon Aurora User Guide . This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Aurora MySQL is available. Amazon Aurora is designed for high performance and availability at global scale with full MySQL compatibility. It provides scale-to-zero serverless compute, Aurora Global Database for multi-Region resilience, Aurora I/O-Optimized for improved price performance on I/O-intensive workloads, and built-in security and continuous backups. To get started, take a look at Aurora's getting started page .
title: Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.4.12 is now generally available

summary: Amazon EventBridge now supports Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) as a target for the enhanced Custom event bus, so you can deliver events to Kafka topics without running your own producer. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. To deliver events to MSK, you create a Subscriber that specifies the cluster ARN and topic. You can also configure Kafka producer settings such as partition key, acknowledgment level, and record headers. EventBridge supports both public and private, serverless and provisioned clusters. When you create a Subscriber for a private cluster, EventBridge automatically sets up a private connection to the cluster. For example, teams that publish to a shared Custom event bus can now deliver purchase-order events to the MSK topics their payments team already consumes from. Amazon MSK targets are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. Delivery to MSK is billed as standard Custom event bus egress. EventBridge also supports compression before delivery, which is billed as an Event Evaluation. To learn more, see Amazon MSK cluster target in the Amazon EventBridge User Guide and the Amazon EventBridge product page . Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Amazon MSK as a target

summary: Amazon EventBridge now supports Webhook Events for the enhanced Custom event bus, so SaaS applications, AI agents, and custom integrations can send events to a bus over HTTPS. You no longer need to deploy and operate your own API endpoint and compute to receive webhooks and publish them to your bus. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. When you create a webhook event source on your bus, EventBridge provides a managed HTTPS URL and verifies each request using an HMAC signature, a static token, or basic authentication. EventBridge then publishes accepted events to the bus, where Subscribers filter and deliver them like any other event. For example, shipment status updates from a logistics partner can reach your order tracking and customer notification Subscribers as soon as the partner sends them. Webhook Events are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. Events received through a webhook are billed as standard Custom event bus ingress, with no additional charge for the webhook. To learn more, see Webhook Events in the Amazon EventBridge User Guide and the Amazon EventBridge product page . Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Webhook Events

summary: AWS CloudFormation StackSets now supports custom execution roles for service-managed stack sets, which enables you to scope the permissions StackSets uses in each target AWS account. StackSets deploys the same infrastructure, such as networking and security settings, across thousands of accounts and Regions in one operation. With a custom execution role, you can also use nested stacks, macros, and transforms in service-managed stack sets, which allows you to deploy the reusable templates you use for individual stacks across your organization. With a custom execution role, you define what StackSets can do in each account. By default, service-managed stack sets use a role in each account that can provision any resource in a template without additional setup, and that default remains available. Now, you can provide a template that defines an IAM role, called the execution role, and StackSets creates it in each account before deploying. For example, a stack set that creates Amazon S3 buckets can use an execution role limited to CloudFormation and Amazon S3 permissions. When you update the execution role template, StackSets updates the role in every account it deployed to. To get started, choose Set execution role when you create a stack set in the CloudFormation console, or use the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit the documentation and the AWS DevOps Blog . This feature is available at no additional charge in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and
title: AWS CloudFormation Service-Managed StackSets adds custom execution roles with nested stacks support

summary: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler expands its AWS SDK integrations with 589 new API actions across 81 AWS services, and adds templated targets for the enhanced EventBridge Custom event bus. You can now schedule direct invocations of a broader set of AWS services without writing custom integration code. EventBridge Scheduler is a serverless scheduler that allows you to create, run, and manage billions of scheduled events and tasks across more than 270 AWS services, without provisioning or managing the underlying infrastructure. With a new templated target, you can schedule event delivery directly to the Custom event bus using its PutEvents or PutRawEvents API. The templated target also makes it easier to add metadata fields to each event. For example, you can send an event to your bus every night at midnight to start a reconciliation workflow, with no function in between to call the API. The new API actions are available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon EventBridge Scheduler is available, subject to the availability of each target service in the Region. The templated targets for the Custom event bus are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. To learn more, see Using templated targets in EventBridge Scheduler and Using universal targets in EventBridge Scheduler in the Amazon EventBridge Scheduler User Guide. Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
title: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler adds 589 new API actions and event bus targets

summary: Today, AWS Billing and Cost Management announces new APIs that let you view your AWS payment information through the AWS SDKs and the AWS CLI. With these APIs, you can check your account balance, find invoices that are due or past due, see which payments and credit memos were applied to each invoice, and confirm that the payment methods on your account are active. You can call the APIs from your own tools or through an AI agent. Previously, finance teams had to sign in to the console to find past-due invoices, match payments to invoices, or check whether a payment method was still active. Now you can automate these checks with APIs such as GetFinancialRecord, BatchGetFinancialRecord, ListFinancialRecords, GetAccountBalance, GetPaymentInstrument and ListPaymentInstruments. You can integrate the APIs with your accounts payable systems to monitor past-due balances and reconcile AWS invoices on your own schedule. The APIs are available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, and available to customers in all commercial AWS Regions. To learn more, visit the AWS Payments API Reference .
title: AWS Billing and Cost Management now offers APIs to track payment status

summary: AWS Pricing Calculator now offers GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost, a new API that returns the estimated cost of a planned workload in a single API call. You send up to 500 usage lines in one request and get the cost back right away, without saving an estimate to your account. While workload estimates let you create and save an estimate in Pricing Calculator, GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost returns a cost on demand, directly in your own tools and workflows. You can choose from three rate types: public On-Demand rates, your rates after discounts, or your rates after discounts plus Savings Plans and Reserved Instances. The API returns the cost of each line and the total. For example, you can check what a design will cost before you deploy it, or let an AI coding agent call the API to price a workload while it helps you design it. GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost is generally available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions, except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, see GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost in the AWS Billing and Cost Management API Reference, or visit the AWS Pricing Calculator product page .
title: AWS Pricing Calculator now estimates workload costs through a new API

summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases, powered by AWS Glue Data Quality, which profiles and evaluates your tables at catalog scale from a single configuration. You define data quality checks once for a catalog, a database, or a single table, and AWS Glue Data Quality evaluates every table in scope, including tables added later, on the cadence you choose. Quality issues surface as data changes, without per-table setup or manual runs, which helps keep bad data from reaching downstream consumers. You can use built-in profiling options that AWS Glue provides for common baseline statistics or provide your own Data Quality Definition Language (DQDL) ruleset with analyzers, rules, or both to hold every table in a database to the same quality standards. You have the flexibility to run evaluations once when you create the configuration or set up triggers, so evaluations run on a schedule or whenever table metadata changes, including every Apache Iceberg commit. After three runs on a table, AWS Glue Data Quality flags anomalous statistics that drift outside expected bounds, surfacing changes that no rule covers. Results are accessible through the existing AWS Glue Data Quality APIs, or you can opt-in to write them to Apache Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog or to Amazon S3. Data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases in AWS Glue Data Catalog is available in all AWS Commercial, AWS GovCloud (US), and AWS China regions. To ge
title: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases

summary: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart now offers a model leaderboard in Amazon SageMaker Studio. You can use it to compare foundation models side by side on throughput, latency, and cost, and then deploy or customize the model that fits your workload. Comparing models has usually meant reading model cards one at a time and relying on benchmark scores that different sources published under different conditions. The JumpStart leaderboard puts consistent measurements in one view. AWS evaluates every model on three reasoning benchmarks, BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA Diamond, and MMLU-Pro, using the same evaluation setup for each model. AWS also measures time to first token, throughput, and instance cost on SageMaker for each JumpStart deployment configuration. You can use all of the filters already available for JumpStart models, such as model provider, license, and input and output modality, to narrow the list. You can also choose a use case profile and an optimization goal (balanced, cost, latency, or throughput) to see the metrics for the configuration you plan to deploy. At launch, the leaderboard covers more than 70 LLMs from providers including Meta, Google, Qwen, IBM, and Arcee. The JumpStart model leaderboard is available at no additional charge in all AWS commercial Regions where Amazon SageMaker Studio is available. To get started, open SageMaker JumpStart in SageMaker Studio and choose the Leaderboard view. To learn more, see JumpStart leaderboard methodology and read the launch blog post
title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart now offers a model leaderboard to compare models on quality, speed, and cost

summary: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles Anywhere now supports aliases, which are readable names that you assign to trust anchors, profiles, and certificate revocation lists (CRLs). Your workloads can request temporary credentials using a trust anchor or profile alias Amazon Resource Name (ARN) instead of an ARN with a system-generated ID, and you can use alias ARNs in many of the operations that manage these resources. Aliases make configurations easier to read and review: an alias ARN that ends in alias/trust-anchor/production-ca can show which certificate authority (CA) a workload uses. Previously, workload configurations, such as credential helper settings in machine images and configuration management templates, referenced trust anchors and profiles by ARNs that contain system-generated IDs, which differ in every account and Region. With this launch, you can assign the same alias in each account and Region, so one configuration template works across them with only the account and Region values changed. To set an alias, specify an alias name when you create, import, or update a resource using the IAM Roles Anywhere console, AWS SDKs, or AWS CLI. This feature is available at no additional cost in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, the China Regions, and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. To learn more, see Using aliases for trust anchors, profiles, and CRLs in the IAM Roles Anywhere User Guide.
title: IAM Roles Anywhere now supports aliases to simplify workload configuration

summary: AWS announces AWS Partner Central guides with access through the AWS Partner Central console and the AWS Partner Central Agents Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. The guides give AWS Partners one place to search, read, and share content that AWS organizes to help partners grow and expand their business. The guides hold authoritative, partner-specific knowledge on programs, benefits, technical topics, marketing, funding, and more, which requires sign-in and permissions. Partners benefit from more accurate answers about programs, benefits, and requirements. Partners can browse by topic, search instantly across every guide, and see content based on their recent activity and AWS program updates. Partners can also ask AWS Partner Central Agents questions in their own words, such as "Which guides explain the requirements for the AWS Foundational Technical Review?" or "Show me everything in Migration Acceleration Program quick reference." Partner Central guides complement the public information about AWS Partner Central features in AWS documentation. AWS Partner Central guides are available to all AWS Partners in the AWS Partner Central console and through the AWS Partner Central Agents MCP server in the US East (N. Virginia) Region in English. Partners can bring these guides into tools such as Kiro, AWS Quick, CRM systems, and other AI clients. To learn more, visit Guides in the AWS Partner Central console or Getting started with the Partner Central Agents MCP server .
title: AWS Partner Central guides now available in the console and through AWS Partner Central Agents

summary: Today, we're announcing third-generation Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file systems, which deliver up to 216 GB/s of throughput and 8.6 million SSD IOPS per file system, up to 3x more throughput and up to 3.6x more SSD IOPS than previous-generation file systems. Built on the latest AWS compute and storage technologies, third-generation file systems give you even more flexibility to scale performance as your workloads and usage patterns evolve. FSx for ONTAP is the first and only storage service that allows you to launch and run fully managed, fully featured ONTAP file systems in the cloud. FSx for ONTAP file systems are powered by up to 12 highly available (HA) pairs of file servers to deliver storage and performance scalability. With previous-generation file systems, each HA pair delivers up to 6 GB/s of throughput and 200,000 SSD IOPS. With third-generation file systems, each HA pair delivers up to 18 GB/s of throughput and 720,000 SSD IOPS, giving you even more flexibility to scale your most demanding ONTAP workloads, such as chip design and verification, media rendering and video editing, and mission-critical databases. FSx for ONTAP third-generation file systems are available today in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio) and US West (Oregon). To learn more, visit the Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP product page and user guide .
title: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP launches a new generation of file systems with up to 3.6x higher performance

summary: Amazon Route 53 now offers Advanced Hosted Zones, a new hosted zone tier with additional guardrails, visibility, and resilience features. Advanced Hosted Zones include Change Guardrails that prevent accidental record deletions, record-level Change History, and public DNS fallback in private hosted zones. A single mistaken DNS change can take part of your domain offline, such as deleting a record that is still serving traffic or removing a delegation that resolvers are still using. To protect against this, customers build their own validation pipelines, review processes, and audit tooling. With Change Guardrails turned on, Route 53 checks each change before applying it. It blocks deleting a record that is still receiving DNS queries, a record that an alias record in the same hosted zone points to, or a delegation that is still in use. When a guardrail blocks a change, Route 53 rejects the whole request with an error that explains why, and no records change. Guardrails apply to every change, including changes from infrastructure as code tools. Change History gives you a record-level history of changes to your hosted zone, retained for 365 days, so you can see what changed and when. To get started, create a new Advanced Hosted Zone or upgrade an existing hosted zone, then turn on the guardrails you want. You can use the Route 53 console, API, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. Advanced Hosted Zones are priced separately from Standard Hosted Zones. For rates, see the Route
title: Amazon Route 53 now offers Advanced Hosted Zones

summary: Amazon Textract Core now lets AI agents extract text, tables, forms, and other data from documents through a skill, with no server to run or infrastructure to deploy. The skill guides an agent to the right Amazon Textract Core API for each document and includes a tested parser that converts the output into reading-order text and structured fields, such as answers to questions, receipt and invoice details, and identity document fields. Previously, teams that connected an agent to Amazon Textract had to build and maintain their own integration. You ask in natural language, and the agent returns the answers you need. The skill processes multi-page PDFs and returns every page in reading order. It uses confidence scores to accept high-confidence results and flags the rest, so you can route them to your own review process. For example, you can ask an agent to turn a patient's intake form into structured data and flag unclear fields for staff review. The skill is available at no additional charge, and standard Amazon Textract pricing applies . It is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon Textract is available, including: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), Europe (Spain), and Europe (Zurich). If you use the AWS MCP server
title: Announcing a new skill for AI agents in Amazon Textract Core

summary: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing (formerly AWS Security Agent) now lets you estimate task hours before running a penetration test, so developers and security teams can see how many billable task hours a test is likely to need and choose a maximum task-hours limit with confidence. Continuum for Penetration Testing runs on-demand, AI-driven penetration tests against your web applications and APIs. Previously, the only way to know how long a test would take was to run it, making it difficult to plan budgets and set appropriate usage limits. With task-hour estimates, you open a penetration test, choose the Pentest cost estimate tab, and request an estimate. AWS Continuum runs a short preliminary analysis of your application's scope. It then draws on expertise from past penetration tests to estimate the task hours needed and shows the task hours that most similar applications finish within, and the higher range a few applications require. Requesting an estimate is free, and the estimate is a guide, not a quote or a limit. Actual task hours can be higher or lower, and only the maximum task-hours limit caps usage. Task-hour estimates are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing is available. To learn more, see the documentation . To get started, visit the AWS Continuum product page .
title: AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing now estimates task hours before you run a test

summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports customer managed keys (CMK) in AWS Key Management Service (KMS) for data encryption at rest. CMK gives you full control over the lifecycle and usage of your KMS keys , helping meet compliance requirements in regulated industries like financial services and healthcare. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. Use MicroVMs to build applications like AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. To get started, create a CMK in AWS KMS and configure its cryptographic properties, metadata, and AWS IAM access permissions. Then, specify this CMK as a parameter when you create a MicroVM image or run a MicroVM. Lambda uses this CMK to encrypt your MicroVM image, MicroVM image environment variables, and the payload passed to the MicroVM run hook. You can use CMK with Lambda MicroVMs through the AWS Lambda console , AWS CloudFormation , AWS Cloud Development Kit , or with your preferred Agentic development tools using the Agent Toolkit for AWS . ​​CMK support for MicroVMs is available in the following AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (Spain), Europe (Stockholm), S
title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports customer managed keys in AWS KMS

summary: AWS Backup now supports incremental backups of Amazon DynamoDB tables, enabling you to reduce backup storage while maintaining backup schedules as frequent as one hour. Until now, AWS Backup created a full copy of your DynamoDB tables. With this launch, after an initial full backup, each incremental backup now captures only the data that changed, and AWS Backup takes a new full backup every 15 days. This lets you store less data and back up more often. You can restore from any recovery point in the chain, and you can schedule incremental backups anywhere from hourly to weekly frequencies. You can store incremental backups in both AWS Backup vaults and logically air-gapped vaults. Cross-Region backup copies are also incremental, further increasing your savings. AWS Backup turns on incremental backups automatically for new customers who protect DynamoDB. If you already back up DynamoDB with AWS Backup, you can turn on incremental backups under advanced features in AWS Backup settings, which lets you manage your backup preferences at the account and region level. You can create and manage incremental backups from the AWS Backup console, the AWS CLI, or the API. Incremental backups for DynamoDB are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Backup protects DynamoDB. To learn more, see working with supported services in the AWS Backup Developer Guide, read the launch blog , and visit the AWS Backup product page . To get started, open the AWS Backup console.
title: AWS Backup now supports incremental backups for Amazon DynamoDB

summary: Amazon Transcribe is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Region. Customers who need to keep data and operations within the EU for regulatory compliance and data sovereignty requirements can now use automatic speech recognition (ASR) in the Region to turn speech into text. Amazon Transcribe offers two ways to transcribe audio in this Region. Batch transcription processes media files stored in Amazon S3, and streaming transcription returns text in real time from live audio over HTTP/2 or WebSocket. Both support custom vocabularies, so you can improve recognition of domain-specific terms such as product names, industry jargon, and proper nouns. To learn more, see Getting started with Amazon Transcribe , Supported languages and language-specific features , and AWS European Sovereign Cloud pricing .
title: Amazon Transcribe now available in AWS European Sovereign Cloud

summary: AWS DevOps Agent now gives you ways to share and leverage skills, MCP servers, connectors, and custom agents that enhance the capabilities of your AWS DevOps Agent instances. The AWS DevOps Agent Tools open source repository is a centralized, AWS-curated collection of tools that extend AWS DevOps Agent capabilities. Customers can import ready-to-use, quality-controlled tools directly into their DevOps Agent configurations to improve investigation quality and expand operational context. A growing community of AWS DevOps Agent users and partners, and AWS service and support teams, have contributed a growing collection of tools to the community, including several partner-managed connectors that simplify connecting AWS DevOps Agent to third party MCP servers. Partners providing connectors include: Bluebox, Bronto, Celonis, Clickhouse Observability, Coralogix, Cribl, Elastic, Halo, Honeycomb, LaunchDarkly, Neo4j, Sumo Logic, and Wiz. To get started, browse the skills and connector catalogs from within your AWS DevOps Agent instance, or add and share your own tools by creating a PR within the AWS DevOps Agent Tools repository. See all the latest AWS DevOps Agent features on the release history page. For the list of AWS Regions where AWS DevOps Agent is available, see the supported Regions table .
title: AWS DevOps Agent adds community and partner tools repository

summary: Amazon Textract Insights brings document understanding to Amazon Textract. It is a new generative AI feature of Amazon Textract, and is now generally available in the US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) AWS Regions. Amazon Textract Insights splits, classifies, and extracts structured data from documents in a single asynchronous request. Documents like insurance claims, tax packets, and onboarding packages often arrive as one long scan that holds many documents in no fixed order. Processing them has meant assembling and operating separate steps for text detection, splitting, classification, and extraction. Amazon Textract Insights handles that work in one managed request, with no AI models to train. How it works: You define the fields you need in a blueprint, a JSON schema that describes each field in natural language, or you can start from a library of AWS public blueprints for common document types such as W-2s, invoices, and bank statements. Amazon Textract Insights can split each file into separate sub-documents, classify each one by matching it to the best-fitting blueprint, and extract your fields. It returns a confidence score for every value and grounds each one to its location on the page, so you can automate high-confidence results and route the rest to human review. It can also return Markdown, HTML, and plain text for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications, generate document summaries and figure captions, and detect and redact personally identifia
title: Amazon Textract Insights is now generally available

summary: When an incident is occurring, mean time to recover needs to be as fast as possible. With this launch, incident investigations performed by AWS DevOps Agent complete faster. Investigations now also include a real-time summary that is updated with the current state of an investigation, so initial findings and observations surface quickly, before a final root cause and mitigation plan are created. For customers using AWS DevOps Agent's built in Slack integration, these summaries are also automatically pushed to the relevant Slack channel. See all the latest AWS DevOps Agent features on the release history page. For the list of AWS Regions where AWS DevOps Agent is available, see the supported Regions table .
title: AWS DevOps Agent reduces investigation latency

summary: Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones now support public DNS fallback. When a query for a name in your private hosted zone's domain doesn't match a record in the zone, Route 53 returns the answer from public DNS instead of a "name not found" (NXDOMAIN) error. Public DNS fallback is part of the Advanced Hosted Zones offering. Until now, Route 53 treated an associated private hosted zone as fully authoritative for its domain, so queries for names that weren't in the zone returned NXDOMAIN. To resolve a few names privately, customers also had to copy every other record from their public zone into the private hosted zone and keep the two in sync. With public DNS fallback, you add only the names you need privately, and every other name resolves from your existing public DNS. For example, your private hosted zone for example.com points example.com to a private endpoint, while partner.example.com exists only in public DNS. Before, a lookup for partner.example.com returned NXDOMAIN. Now it resolves from public DNS. To get started, create a private Advanced Hosted Zone or upgrade an existing private hosted zone, and then turn on public DNS fallback. You can use the Route 53 console, API, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. Public DNS fallback is available in all AWS commercial Regions where Route 53 private hosted zones are available. To learn more, see Enabling public DNS fallback for a private hosted zone in the Route 53 Developer Guide and the Route 53 pricing page .
title: Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones now support public DNS fallback

summary: AWS DevOps Agent now extends its chat capabilities across MCP clients like Kiro and Claude Code, as well as Slack and Microsoft Teams channels. With Model Context Protocol (MCP) support, AWS DevOps Agent can now take directed chat actions including support for GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, and PagerDuty MCP tools, giving developers and operations teams powerful workflow automation directly from their preferred chat interface. This launch also adds auto-creation of per-incident Slack code channels and bi-directional chat within Microsoft Teams. AWS DevOps Agent has access to a compute sandbox that it can use to execute scripts and access the network to work more efficiently, and users can now rename and archive chats across all supported platforms. See all the latest AWS DevOps Agent features on the release history page. For the list of AWS Regions where AWS DevOps Agent is available, see the supported Regions table .
title: AWS DevOps Agent adds new chat capabilities

summary: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks are now supported in the AWS Asia Pacific (Osaka) Region. Outposts racks extend AWS infrastructure, AWS services, APIs, and tools to virtually any on-premises data center or colocation space for a truly consistent hybrid experience. Organizations of every size, from startups to enterprises to public sector agencies, can now order Outposts racks connected to this newly supported Region to optimize for latency and data residency needs. This regional expansion provides additional flexibility in the number of AWS Regions that customers' Outposts can connect to. To learn more about second-generation Outposts racks, read the AWS Outposts blog post and user guide . For the latest list of countries and territories and the AWS Regions where second-generation Outposts racks are supported, see the AWS Outposts FAQs page .
title: Second-generation AWS Outposts racks now supported in the AWS Asia Pacific (Osaka)

summary: Improved blueprints: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now gives project teams more ownership of their data and resources, within governance policies that administrators set centrally. Additional releases include faster notebook queries through DuckDB 2.0 support and data quality monitoring at catalog scale. Improved data quality monitoring: Teams can also profile entire catalogs and databases to keep data statistics current. Project members can get email notifications for all supported notification types, including data quality and data profiling runs. Improved catalog experience: Administrators can now manage metadata forms, business glossaries, and custom asset types in one place, with a consistent experience across all domain types. They can also transfer asset ownership to the project that knows the data best. Members of that project can then curate those assets and approve or reject subscription requests themselves. With resource blueprints, administrators can allow projects to deploy approved resources, such as Amazon EMR Serverless applications. Teams can then provision what they need without waiting for an administrator. Support for DuckDB 2.0 and extensions: SageMaker notebooks now support DuckDB 2.0 and DuckDB extensions. Data engineers, analysts, and data scientists get faster queries over Amazon S3 data, plus access to more file formats, data source connectors, and functions such as excel, geospatial and full-text search. These capabilities are available in all AWS
title: Amazon SageMaker adds new capabilities – improved blueprints and catalog experience, simplified data quality monitoring, and support for DuckDB 2.0 and DuckDB extensions

summary: The AWS Secrets Store CSI Driver Provider now supports AssumeRole (role-chaining), allowing Kubernetes pods to access secrets and parameters across AWS accounts by assuming an IAM role in the account where the secrets are stored. Previously, customers reading cross-account secrets needed to add a resource policy to each secret and use a customer-managed KMS key, as the AWS managed key (aws/secretsmanager) cannot be used for cross-account access.
